title: High-Frequency Enhancement and Dual-Model Ensemble for Language-Guided COVID-19 Pneumonia Lesion Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of COVID-19 pneumonia lesions in chest X-ray (CXR) images is critical for disease quantification and clinical decision-making. However, existing methods suffer from blurred lesion boundaries, missed detection of tiny lesions, and limited generalization performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a language-guided multimodal medical image segmentation method integrating high-frequency enhancement and a dual-model ensemble. The method is developed along three dimensions: frequency-domain detail enhancement, spatial alignment optimization, and dual-model ensemble. First, a frequency-domain decomposition-based high-frequency enhancement module is designed to mitigate detail attenuation caused by encoder downsampling. Second, a two-dimensional (2D) spatial position encoding module is introduced to improve the spatial alignment between text descriptions and visual regions. Third, a dual-model ensemble architecture with differentiated frequency-domain masks is constructed to address the performance ceiling of individual models. Finally, experiments on two public datasets with different imaging modalities and data characteristics demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing single-modal and multimodal baseline methods and achieves competitive performance comparable to state-of-the-art approaches, verifying the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework. On the QaTa-COV19 dataset, the Dice coefficient reaches 91.85% and the mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) reaches 84.98%. On the multi-institutional MosMedData+ dataset, the Dice coefficient reaches 78.48% and the mIoU reaches 64.66%. The proposed method provides effective technical support for clinical diagnosis and follow-up assessment of pneumonia.

title: DAPNet: a decoupled adaptive prototyping network for few-shot medical image segmentation.
abstract: Few-shot medical image segmentation (FSMIS) holds immense potential in medical scenarios where annotations are expensive and scarce. However, the majority of existing methods perform queries under the guidance of a foreground prototype, which causes them to struggle, as this single representation fails to effectively model both the target and its complex anatomical surroundings. To address this limitation, we propose the decoupled adaptive prototype network (DAPNet), explicitly disentangling the representation of foreground and background through a dual-path dynamic feature enhancement and feedback framework. The deformable anatomical prototype sampling (DAPS) module, which innovatively combines coordinate-aware and deformable convolutions to achieve adaptive anatomical alignment, resulting in a robust set of background prototypes derived from support features; and the dual attention-boosted prototyping module, which generates a highly discriminative foreground prototype by fusing semantic attention with a boundary-aware mechanism to effectively mitigate feature bias and enhance the structural integrity of the target. By jointly optimizing these distinct but complementary prototypes, DAPNet forms a powerful and comprehensive representation for classification. Extensive experiments on multiple public datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches. Ablation studies and visualizations further validate the effectiveness and synergy of our proposed modules, establishing a new and robust paradigm for FSMIS.

title: Quantitative Measurement of White Matter Hyperintensities in Brain MRI using a Multimodal Boundary-Aware Dual-Task Segmentation Framework.
abstract: White matter hyperintensity (WMH) subtype segmentation in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains challenging due to heterogeneous lesion sizes, indistinct boundaries, and severe class imbalance. We propose a multimodal boundary-aware dual-task U-Net for segmenting periventricular (PVWMH), deep (DWMH), and subcortical (SWMH) lesions. The framework integrates FLAIR-T1-weighted feature fusion, Vision Mamba-based feature modeling, an SWMH-specific boundary loss, and auxiliary boundary detection. The method was evaluated using patient-level five-fold cross-validation on a private multicenter cohort (n = 75) and separately on 60 publicly annotated MICCAI WMH Challenge subjects for binary segmentation. On the private cohort, the proposed framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.6081 and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 14.80 mm, compared with 0.5638 and 18.25 mm for the FLAIR-only ablation baseline. It also improved SWMH DSC from 0.4610 with nnU-Net to 0.5215 (p = 0.008). On the public dataset, the mean binary DSC and HD95 were 0.6812 and 12.91 mm, respectively.Given the relatively large through-plane voxel spacing (8.4 mm), the framework processes 2D axial slices independently and does not explicitly model inter-slice context, which may limit its ability to characterize lesions extending across adjacent slices.

title: Meaningful thresholds for change in quantitative computed tomography-derived fibrosis extent in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
abstract: Rationale Validated thresholds for clinically meaningful change in quantitative computed tomography (QCT) for fibrosis extent across algorithms remain unclear in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Objectives To evaluate minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for 1-year change in QCT metrics in IPF using different algorithms than previously reported and to identify prognostically meaningful thresholds for effective risk stratification. Methods This multicenter retrospective study included IPF patients with baseline and 1-year follow-up CT. Minimal clinically important differences for change in fibrosis score (ΔFS) derived from fully automated CT quantification were estimated using an anchor-based approach with 1-year changes in FVC and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLco), and a prognostic threshold was estimated using maximally selected log-rank statistics. Prognostic significance of ΔFS was evaluated in discovery and validation cohorts. Results The discovery cohort included 524 patients (mean age = 66.8 years; 79% men), and the external validation cohort included 224 patients (mean age = 69.6 years; 83% men). Anchor-based MCIDs were 2.72% for FVC and 4.52% for DLco, with a prognostic threshold of 4.05%. In the discovery cohort, 1-year ΔFS were independently associated with transplant-free survival (TFS), with greater risk when ΔFS exceeded MCID or prognostic thresholds (all, P < .001). In the validation cohort, ΔFS remained associated with TFS (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 1.11; 95% CI, 1.04-1.18), and all prespecified ΔFS thresholds were prognostic for overall TFS, with the prognostic threshold of ΔFS ≥ 4.05% showing the most consistent associations with overall (aHR = 2.78; 95% CI, 1.36-5.68) and 3-year TFS (aHR = 2.88; 95% CI, 1.11-7.48). Conclusion One-year change in FS and its thresholds were significantly associated with TFS, supporting annual CT follow-up with predefined QCT thresholds for monitoring and risk stratification in IPF.

title: An update to the classification, evaluation, and management of childhood interstitial lung disease in infancy: an official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline.
abstract: Background Childhood interstitial lung diseases (chILD) are a heterogeneous group of rare disorders. In 2013, the American Thoracic Society (ATS) developed a guideline regarding the classification, evaluation, and management of children <2 years old with chILD. The current guideline provides updated recommendations regarding genetic testing, chest imaging, lung biopsy, and lung transplant referral. Methods The Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach was used to form clinical questions, summarize evidence, and develop recommendations, following ATS policies and procedures. A multidisciplinary panel with expertise in chILD formulated recommendations addressing diagnostic tools and referral for lung transplant evaluation. Results Rapid and broad genetic testing is recommended for infants with chILD and respiratory failure (strong recommendation). Chest computed tomography (CT) remains an important part of the diagnostic evaluation (conditional recommendation). Surgical lung biopsy is recommended when there is urgency to identify a specific chILD disorder and genetic testing is not feasible, timely, or inconclusive; to identify histopathologic "treatable traits"; or to inform prognosis (strong recommendation). Referral for lung transplant evaluation is recommended for children with specific chILD disorders with predictable poor outcomes (strong recommendation). Repeat chest CT to aid decision-making, prognosis, and/or change therapies is suggested for children with chILD diagnosed before age 2 years (conditional recommendation). Conclusions This guideline provides evidence-based recommendations for genetic testing, chest imaging, lung biopsy, and referral for lung transplant evaluation to improve the diagnostic evaluation and management of children <2 years with chILD. Implementing this guideline will hopefully increase genetic testing for chILD, inform the diagnostic evaluation and disease monitoring of chILD, and identify future research priorities for chILD.

title: Geo-economic variations in structure and organization of intensive care units: the ISOREA survey.
abstract: Purpose Little is known on critical care services globally. This study aimed to describe ICU resources and organization across countries and assess variability by income group, between countries, and within countries. Methods Participating centers provided structured data on hospital and ICU characteristics via electronic case report form (January 2018 to July 2020). title: Serial Mass Tuberculosis Screening Among the Elderly in Eastern China from 2021-2023.
abstract: Rationale The impact of repeated community-wide tuberculosis screening is uncertain because evidence from large-scale, multi-round screening campaigns is limited. Objectives We evaluated whether annual, community-based, chest-radiography screening was associated with reduced tuberculosis prevalence and detection of asymptomatic disease across multiple screening rounds. Methods We conducted three annual chest X-ray screening rounds (2021-2023) among adults aged ≥60 years in Lanxi City, Zhejiang Province. All participants underwent chest radiography at community health centers, with referral for diagnostic evaluation and bacteriological testing. We estimated detection yields per 100,000 screened persons, assessed trends, and used direct standardization and repeated-participation analyses. Measurements and main results Across all rounds, 214,948 screening encounters were completed. From Round 1 to Round 3, screening-detected prevalence declined for overall tuberculosis (233.1 [95% CI, 194.2-279.7] to 146.3 [95% CI, 123.1-173.9] per 100,000 screened persons) and bacteriologically-confirmed tuberculosis (162.1 [95% CI, 130.3-201.7] to 108.6 [95% CI, 88.8-132.7] per 100,000 screened persons). From Round 1 to Round 3, asymptomatic tuberculosis decreased as both a proportion of cases (47.8% to 26.6%) and prevalence among screened participants (111.5 to 38.9 per 100,000). Compared with Round 1, tuberculosis prevalence was lower in Round 2 (-28.1% change; 95% CI, -44.0 to - 7.5) and Round 3 (-37.2% change; 95% CI, -51.2 to - 19.2). The Round 2-to-Round 3 difference was smaller and included the null (-12.8% change; 95% CI, -31.7 to 11.4). Standardization and repeated-participation analyses yielded broadly similar patterns. Conclusions Serial community-level screening was associated with declining tuberculosis prevalence, including asymptomatic disease, with the largest reduction occurring between the first and second screening rounds.

title: Withdrawn as duplicate: Pulmonary Blood Volumes on CT Predict Residual Pulmonary Hypertension Post-Pulmonary Endarterectomy.
abstract: Pulmonary blood volumes (PBV), currently not assessed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA), could provide additional information to routine investigations performed for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). We investigated CTPA-based PBV in evaluating hemodynamic outcome from pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) surgery. A deep learning-based CTPA vascular segmentation model, differentiating arteries and veins, was applied for automated PBV measurements in CTEPH patients who underwent PEA at U.K.'s national CTEPH service. Pulmonary arteries were compartmentalised into "central" (main pulmonary and proximal lobar) and "intrapulmonary". Mean pulmonary arterial pressure >30 mmHg post-PEA defined "clinically relevant" residual PH. Logistic regression models applying CTPA-based PBV to identify residual PH were trained and tested on the discovery and validation cohorts respectively. Paired pre- and postoperative CTPA, in the discovery (n = 71) and validation (n = 102) cohorts showed that central pulmonary artery volume and total artery to vein volume ratio (A-VR) decreased and pulmonary vein volume increased with hemodynamic improvement post-PEA. Preoperative central pulmonary artery volume and A-VR helped identify patients at risk for clinically relevant residual PH post-PEA (AUROC 0.88 and 0.82 in the discovery and validation cohorts). Postoperative central pulmonary artery volume, A-VR and pulmonary vein volume helped to non-invasively identify patients without clinically relevant residual PH (AUROC 0.91 and 0.88 in the discovery and validation cohorts). Automated quantification of CTPA-based PBV at diagnosis can help stratify risk for residual PH in patients managed with PEA. Utilizing CTPA-derived PBV post-PEA to identify patients without residual PH can potentially reduce the need for routine postoperative right heart catheterization.

title: Regional micro-computed tomography analysis enables longitudinal detection of compensatory ventilation effects in a mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis.
abstract: Accurate lung function assessment is essential in preclinical idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) research, yet conventional whole-lung endpoints overlook spatial heterogeneity and compensatory mechanisms. We present a micro-computed tomography (µCT)-based pipeline for longitudinal, regional quantification of structural and functional changes in a murine bleomycin (BLM)-induced fibrosis model to improve evaluation of disease progression and therapeutic effects. C57BL/6 mice received triple oropharyngeal administrations of saline or BLM. Respiratory-gated µCT scans were acquired in free-breathing at baseline and days 7, 14, and 21. A deep-learning algorithm segmented the lungs into left and right lobes, further subdivided into apical and caudal regions using airway landmarks. Regional volumes, aeration compartments, and ventilation maps were extracted to assess structural and functional alterations. Saline-treated mice showed stable metrics over time, with minimal interanimal variability, demonstrating the robustness and physiological consistency of our segmentation procedure. BLM-treated animals exhibited early and heterogeneous fibrotic changes, with the apical regions appearing as most affected. The caudal-right region displayed a compensatory functional increase of respiratory parameters derived from multivolume µCT. µCT-based regional analysis can detect localized dysfunction and compensatory effects not captured by whole-lung measurements. This strategy is applicable to different models of heterogeneous lung disease and may contribute to reduce the translational gap in IPF research.

title: Quantitative CT in the real-world evaluation of progressive pulmonary fibrosis; the REVISE PPF multicentre observational study.
abstract: Rationale and objective We assessed whether an FDA-cleared quantitative CT (qCT) tool (Brainomix, e-Lung) identifies progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) earlier than routine clinical diagnosis and evaluated the prognostic value of baseline and serial imaging biomarkers. Methods Multicentre retrospective study involving University of Alabama (UAB), Weill Cornell Medicine (WCM) and University of Chicago (UChicago); n = 509. HRCTs were analysed with e-Lung to derive Weighted Reticulovascular Score (WRVS, %), Total Disease Extent (TDE, %), and e-Lung Volume (mL). Prespecified progression thresholds were an absolute WRVS increase of ≥ 3 percentage points, an absolute TDE increase of ≥ 1.5 percentage points, and a relative e-Lung Volume decline of ≥ 10%, over less than 2 years. We compared the earliest qCT progression date with recorded clinical PPF diagnoses, assessed clinically stable controls, and modelled associations with future PPF and mortality using adjusted time-varying Cox models. Results Among 200 patients with PPF and serial HRCTs meeting the prespecified timing criterion, qCT identified progression earlier in 78% (UAB), 83% (WCM), and 47% (UChicago), with mean lead times of 434, 847, and 220 days, respectively. Among 187 clinically stable patients meeting the same serial-imaging criterion, progression thresholds were met in 67%, 56%, and 42%, respectively. High-risk baseline WRVS (≥15%) predicted future PPF (OR 4.09, 2.48, and 2.30) and mortality (HR 2.03 pooled UAB/WCM; 2.75 UChicago). Per 1-percentage-point increase, adjusted mortality HRs were 1.15 and 1.19 for WRVS and 1.05 and 1.04 for TDE in pooled UAB/WCM and UChicago, respectively. Threshold crossings were also associated with mortality (WRVS: HR 6.50 pooled UAB/WCM, 4.05 UChicago; TDE: 7.60 and 3.26; e-Lung Volume: 8.20 and 2.59). Conclusion qCT detects radiological progression months to years before clinical PPF diagnoses. Integrating e-Lung into ILD pathways could accelerate treatment decisions and personalize follow-up.

title: Evaluation of Costal Cartilage Calcification Using Plain Radiographic Images.
abstract: Background Costal cartilage is a vital autologous graft for structural rhinoplasty, but calcification complicates surgical planning and graft manipulation. Chest computed tomography is the conventional evaluation method but is not routinely used owing to radiation exposure and cost. Objectives To evaluate, using plain rib series radiography, the prevalence, morphological patterns, and predictors of costal cartilage calcification in patients undergoing rhinoplasty. Methods Two reviewers jointly assessed bilateral 6th-8th costal cartilages from 183 rhinoplasty patients (1,098 rib segments) on preoperative chest radiographs, grading calcification (0-4) and classifying morphological pattern (marginal, granular, or central). Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of calcification presence and severity. Results Costal cartilage calcification (grade ≥1) was present in 54.1% of segments, with significantly higher prevalence (62.9% vs 46.6%, P < 0.001) and severity in females than males. Calcification was predominantly marginal in males (95.4%), whereas 15.1% and 17.6% of females showed granular and central patterns, respectively. Severe calcification (grade ≥3) peaked unexpectedly in the 40-49-year group (25.8%) rather than in older patients. On multivariable analysis, female sex (OR 3.01; 95% CI, 1.11-8.12) and age 40-49 years (OR 6.28; 95% CI, 1.69-23.36) were independent predictors of severe calcification. Conclusions Routine rib series imaging should be considered even in younger candidates to optimize donor site selection and avoid unexpected intraoperative findings.

title: RibXcar: Safety Fundamentals and Surgical Protocol for Controlled Costal Osteotomy in Body Contouring Surgery: A Prospective Study of 100 Patients.
abstract: Background Aesthetic body contouring surgery has incorporated costal modification techniques to improve waist definition. The lack of standardized protocols and prospective safety data has generated controversy. The RibXcar technique proposes a controlled monocortical costal osteotomy as an alternative to rib resection; however, no prospective studies have comprehensively evaluated its safety profile. Objectives To describe a standardized surgical protocol for the RibXcar technique and prospectively evaluate its safety, efficacy, impact on pulmonary function, postoperative pain, and patient satisfaction. Methods A prospective study of 100 consecutive patients who underwent RibXcar alone (n=80) or combined with body liposuction (n=20). A 10-step protocol was described, and outcomes were evaluated: complications, pulmonary function (spirometry), waist diameter, costal angulation (ultrasound), pain (VAS), and satisfaction (Body-Q) preoperatively and at 6 months. Results The overall minor complication rate was 8%, with no cases of pneumothorax or hemothorax. Pulmonary function showed no significant changes at 6 months in either group. Waist diameter reduction was 5.0 cm (IQR: 3.75-7.0) in the RibXcar group and 10.50 ± 1.73 cm in the combined group (P < .001). Costal angulation decreased significantly in all evaluated ribs (P < .0001). Body-Q scores improved significantly (P < .00001), and pain resolved by 6 months. Conclusions The results of this series suggest that RibXcar, when performed under a standardized protocol, may constitute a safe and effective alternative for aesthetic rib remodeling in selected patients. The preservation of pulmonary function and the low complication rate observed would support its implementation in advanced body contouring surgery.

title: XCREST II: The X-factor in Iliac Crest Remodeling for Advanced Waist-to-hip Definition.
abstract: Background Modern body contouring has evolved toward structural reshaping, with the waist-hip-gluteal unit as a key determinant of body contour aesthetics. The iliac crest is a critical landmark for lower waist contour. Objectives To evaluate the aesthetic outcomes, safety, and anatomical contribution of XCREST II, a combined bony and myofascial technique for lower waist contouring. Methods A multicenter retrospective cohort study included 480 patients who underwent XCREST II between 2024 and 2026. Patients were categorized into four groups: XCREST II alone (n = 180), XCREST II + gluteal fat grafting (n = 84), XCREST II + RibXcar (n = 132), and XCREST II + RibXcar + gluteal fat grafting (n = 84). All underwent ultrasound-guided iliac crest remodeling with partial gluteus medius detachment. Anthropometric and BODY-Q outcomes were assessed preoperatively and at 12 months. Results Four hundred eighty patients were included. Baseline characteristics were comparable, except for longer operative time in combined procedures (p < 0.001). At 12 months, all anthropometric measures improved significantly from baseline across groups (p < 0.001), without intergroup differences. Complications were low; prolonged postoperative pain and iliac crest pain were more frequent in groups including RibXCar (p = 0.020 and p = 0.017, respectively), without chronic pain. BODY-Q scores improved significantly across all domains (p < 0.001), differing only in body image (p = 0.019) and scar assessment (p < 0.001). Conclusions XCREST II, a refinement of XCREST incorporating partial gluteus medius detachment, demonstrated favorable 12-month waist contour improvement and high patient satisfaction, with a low complication rate. Outcomes were consistent across subgroups.

title: Breast Implant Flipping: Prevalence, Clinical Correlation, and Independent Risk Factors in a Consecutive Ultrasound Cohort.
abstract: Background Silicone breast implants are designed with an anterior domed surface, and relatively flat posterior surface that contains the cured silicone patch. With implant flipping (an anterior-posterior malposition), the posterior patch rotates to an anterior position. Objectives There are currently no prospective published studies reporting the prevalence of implant flipping and its associated symptoms in aesthetic patients. This prospective study used in-office high-resolution ultrasound (HRUS) to evaluate the prevalence of breast implant flipping, assess associated changes in breast shape, appearance, and symptoms, and identify potential risk factors. Methods Consecutive patients with silicone breast implants presenting for routine follow-up underwent HRUS at 7 study sites in the United States over a 4-month period between April 1st and August 1st, 2026. Demographic data included age and BMI. Implant data included time since surgery, whether a primary of revision procedure, number of revisions, manufacturer, size, style, surface, use of ADM or scaffold, pocket location, capsule grade, flipped or not, and rupture. Results Five hundred and ninety consecutive patients were enrolled over 4 months. Mean age 43 years with range 22-82, mean BMI 23 with range of 16-34.5. Primary augmentations accounted for 64.6% of procedures, while revision augmentations accounted for 35.4%. Device manufacturer distribution, 63.9% Allergan, 12.4% Mentor, 15.9% Motiva, and 7.1% Sientra. Implant flipping was identified in 75 patients (12.7%). Conclusions Implant flipping was identified by HRUS in one in eight patients. Larger implant volume, prepectoral placement, and lack of soft tissue support were independently associated with flipping. HRUS improves detection, patient counseling, and surgical planning.

title: RED Protocol: Ultrasound for Intraoperative Detection of Pneumothorax and Hemothorax in Rib Remodeling Surgeries.
abstract: Background Ribcage remodeling procedures are increasingly used in aesthetic surgery to reduce waist circumference; however, they carry a potential risk of pneumothorax and hemothorax due to proximity to the lung parenchyma. Early intraoperative detection of these complications is critical but currently not standardized. Objectives To evaluate the feasibility and diagnostic performance of the Rib Complication Evaluation and Detection (RED) protocol, an intraoperative ultrasound-based approach for detecting pneumothorax and hemothorax during ribcage remodeling procedures. Methods A retrospective observational study was conducted including 113 patients undergoing ribcage remodeling between 2023 and 2024. Due to the low incidence of pneumothorax, the protocol was additionally assessed using 250 high-fidelity simulation scenarios with the CAE Vimedix system. Ultrasound findings were standardized, and sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values were calculated. Results No cases of pneumothorax or hemothorax were identified in the clinical cohort. In simulation testing, the RED protocol demonstrated a sensitivity of 96% and specificity of 100% for pneumothorax detection, with a positive predictive value of 100% and a negative predictive value of 98%. The protocol successfully differentiated pneumothorax from other thoracic conditions. Conclusions The RED protocol provides a structured and reproducible approach for intraoperative lung ultrasound in ribcage remodeling. While simulation was necessary due to the low prevalence of complications, the protocol is based on well-established sonographic signs. Its high negative predictive value suggests utility as a rule-out tool, enhancing intraoperative safety. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its performance in real clinical scenarios.

title: Epicardial and pericardial adipose tissue: anatomy, physiology, imaging, segmentation, and treatment effects.
abstract: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) and pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) are increasingly recognized as distinct fat depots with implications for cardiovascular disease. This review discusses their anatomical and physiological characteristics, as well as their pathophysiological roles. EAT, in direct contact with the myocardium, exerts local inflammatory and metabolic effects on the heart, while PAT influences cardiovascular health rather systemically. We sought to discuss the currently used imaging modalities to assess these fat compartments-CT, MRI, and echocardiography-emphasizing their advantages, limitations, and the urgent need for standardization for both scanning and image reconstruction. Advances in image segmentation, particularly deep learning-based approaches, have improved the accuracy and reproducibility of EAT and PAT quantification. This review also explores the role of EAT and PAT as risk factors for cardiovascular outcomes, summarizing conflicting evidence across studies. Finally, we summarize the effects of medical therapy and lifestyle interventions on reducing EAT volume. Understanding and accurately quantifying EAT and PAT is essential for cardiovascular risk stratification and may open new pathways for therapeutic interventions.

title: Coronary computed tomography angiography as a screening tool.
abstract: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) has evolved into a key non-invasive tool for evaluating coronary artery disease, offering high sensitivity, detailed anatomical visualization, and strong prognostic value. Current Society of Cardiovascular Computed Tomography guidelines recommend CCTA as a first-line test for symptomatic patients, while limiting its use in asymptomatic individuals to select high-risk cases. Advantages in a screening context include early detection of subclinical atherosclerosis, prognostic assessment through high-risk plaque features, and facilitation of personalized preventive strategies. However, widespread screening faces challenges: procedural complexity, contrast and radiation exposure, psychological impact, and economic cost. Emerging integration of artificial intelligence promises to enhance efficiency, automate plaque quantification, and enable individualized risk prediction, potentially improving cost-effectiveness and clinical adoption. Future validation through randomized controlled trials and real-world data is needed to confirm the impact of CCTA-based screening on cardiovascular event reduction, healthcare resource use, and patient quality of life.

title: Extracardiac imaging biomarkers of cardiovascular health: a comprehensive review.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading global cause of morbidity and mortality. Beyond clinical risk factors and cardiac imaging, extracardiac imaging biomarkers provide complementary insight into cardiometabolic health. Routine non-cardiac imaging often depicts the liver, kidneys, pancreas, lung, brain, adipose tissue, muscle, vasculature, breast, and bone, enabling opportunistic risk assessment. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), detectable on MRI, CT, and ultrasound, independently predicts major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Chronic kidney disease-related markers including kidney size, vascular calcification, and renal resistive index also correlate with adverse outcomes. Reduced pancreas volume is similarly associated with cardiovascular disease. CT-quantified emphysema and lung hyperinflation are associated with coronary artery disease and cardiovascular mortality. Cerebral small vessel disease markers, such as white matter hyperintensities and silent brain infarcts, demonstrate associations with cardiovascular events. Ectopic adiposity and sarcopenia quantified by CT, MRI, and ultrasound add prognostic value beyond body mass index. Extracardiac vascular and skeletal biomarkers, such as breast arterial calcification and low bone mineral density, further associate with cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Collectively, these markers improve risk stratification and enable screening without added cost or radiation. Future priorities include standardization, external validation, and integration into risk prediction models to advance precision cardiovascular medicine.

title: Optimization and technological advances in cardiovascular magnetic resonance to improve access and screening.
abstract: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) can comprehensively assess cardiac function and structure, with a unique capability for tissue characterization. However, its access remains limited due to general availability. Additionally, CMR has lengthy preparation and acquisition times. Various optimization methods and techniques have been proposed to streamline CMR workflow and shorten total acquisition times. These include patient preparation, rapid imaging protocols, sequences developments, deep learning-based image acceleration and reconstruction, as well as automated image analysis and report generation. Together, these advances may grant CMR access to more patients and even enable more accessible non-invasive cardiac screening of high-risk and general population in the future. This narrative review provides an overview of different concepts and technologies aiming at optimizing CMR in terms of workflow and image acquisition and highlights the opportunities for high-volume CMR studies to support more patient-centred cardiovascular care.

title: Pericoronary adipose tissue imaging: quantitative assessment, artificial intelligence integration, and therapeutic modulation.
abstract: Pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) is increasingly recognised as a biosensor of vascular inflammation. The guideline-driven widespread adoption of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) as the first-line investigation for coronary artery disease (CAD) has created opportunities for evaluating the inflammatory burden through quantitative assessment of PCAT. Standardising raw PCAT imaging data for technical, anatomical, and biological variability provides the Fat-Attenuation Index (FAI) Score, which shows promise as a metric of coronary inflammation. Quantification of coronary inflammation has implications for the diagnosis, risk stratification, and monitoring of treatment in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. This review examines the anatomical and physiological basis of PCAT, highlighting the importance of standardising PCAT imaging for the implementation as a clinical biomarker, and reviews the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enhancing precision and scalability. Emerging evidence on the modulation of FAI Score by therapeutic agents, including statins, biologics, and cardiometabolic drugs, and the potential utility of serial imaging in guiding clinical care is also discussed. With ongoing large-scale validation and emerging AI -based approaches, PCAT imaging is poised to complement traditional risk factors and plaque metrics; however, current evidence remains evolving, and the integration of inflammatory risk assessment could be useful to guide emerging anti-inflammatory treatments in personalised cardiovascular medicine.
authorString: Eveson L, Sobirov I, Chan K.

title: Coronary artery calcium score-emerging role for opportunistic screening on thoracic CT and novel applications.
abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) can be identified on thoracic CT performed for a variety of clinical indications, including routine thoracic CT, lung cancer screening CT, and attenuation correction CT. Identification of CAC on thoracic CT as part of opportunistic screening can improve the assessment of cardiovascular risk and can identify patients who may benefit from preventative medical therapies. This approach enhances early detection of coronary artery disease within existing healthcare workflows. However, at present, there are no randomized trials that assess the clinical impact of this approach. Recently, the development of artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) models has facilitated the automated identification and quantification of CAC, offering rapid and reproducible assessments. Artificial intelligence/machine learning models could reduce radiologist workload and provide end-to-end integration into routine clinical practice. Novel technologies such as photon-counting CT offer further potential for CAC detection and risk stratification through the use of high-resolution imaging and spectral imaging with virtual non-contrast images. This review discusses the evidence for opportunistic screening for CAC on thoracic CT and highlights novel applications including AI/ML assessments, CAC as a multi-system biomarker, and the potential for photon counting CT.

title: Advanced quantitative CT for coronary artery disease: integrating stenosis quantification, plaque quantification, and fractional flow reserve-CT.
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) continues to be a leading cause of death globally. Radiological evaluation of CAD generally consists of stenosis detection by cardiac CT angiography (CCTA). However, this approach can be inefficient and subject to interobserver variability. In this review, we explore the newest developments related to CAD evaluation by CCTA, with an emphasis on plaque quantification. Artificial intelligence-based quantitative CT offers an efficient and reproducible method to analyze plaque biomarkers that support more refined risk stratification for major adverse cardiovascular events. Artificial intelligence-based coronary stenosis quantification can streamline workflow and improve consistency. The utilization of a photon-counting detector CT has been demonstrated to enhance spatial resolution, thereby allowing more precise coronary lumen analysis and artifact reduction. Fractional flow reserve-CT delivers a noninvasive physiologic assessment of stenotic lesions. Finally, we discuss the impact of these changes on risk stratification and guiding preventive therapy as well as possible future directions in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Incidental pulmonary embolism and the value of CT pulmonary angiography follow-up versus expert review.
abstract: Objectives Evaluate the prevalence of true-positive and false-positive incidental pulmonary embolism (iPE) diagnoses and the impact of expert review on diagnostic accuracy. Methods This single-center retrospective study included consecutive contrast-enhanced thoracic CT examinations without dedicated PE protocols which reported iPE over an 18-month period (2022-24). Electronic health records were reviewed to identify requests to confirm PE based on previous non-dedicated studies. Studies identifying iPE were graded from 1 (most certain) to 5 by original report diagnostic certainty and compared between PE-positive and PE-negative subgroups using Fisher's exact test. Identified imaging received retrospective expert review to calculate expert agreement with CTPA, where CTPA had been performed, using Cohen's kappa. Results Of 25 214 CT examinations, 260 (1%) reported iPE (mean age 73 ± 12 years; 51% women). Of these, 25% (n = 65/260) underwent confirmatory CTPA. Patients receiving CTPA had lower initial iPE diagnostic certainty (median 3 versus 1, P < .01) and 52% (n = 34/65) were PE-positive on CTPA. Patients with false-positive diagnoses had reduced diagnostic certainty on non-dedicated studies compared to those with a true-positive diagnosis (median 3 versus 2, P < .001). Agreement between the expert review of the iPE scan and the ground-truth CTPA diagnosis had κ of 0.96. Conclusions Expert review could be an effective tool to reduce CTPA requirement in cases of intermediate (grade 3) iPE diagnostic certainty. Advances in knowledge Low-certainty incidental pulmonary embolism diagnoses on initial non-dedicated CT are more likely to be false-positives according to CTPA findings or expert thoracic radiologist review. Expert review of initial CT may therefore reduce excessive imaging and avoid treating false-positive cases.

title: Ultrasound evaluation and outcome of breast masses in a cohort of pubertal children.
abstract: Objective To describe the ultrasound evaluation and outcome of breast masses in a cohort of pubertal children. Methods A single institution, institutional review board-approved, retrospective study was performed including 13- to 18-year-old patients who had a breast ultrasound from January 1990 to December 2024. Clinical information and the ultrasound results were collected. Ultrasound was deemed positive if it explained the patients' concern. Tissue sample was determined by the patient and ordering physician. Pathology results and follow-up ultrasounds were recorded as well. Descriptive analysis was performed. Results Two hundred forty patients (237 females) were included with a mean age of 17 years. The most common indication was a palpable mass (65%). Two hundred thirty-seven ultrasounds were positive (99%), 193 patients had a biopsy (80%). The most common diagnoses were fibroadenoma (69%), hamartoma (13%), and phyllodes tumor (7%). No primary or secondary breast malignancies were identified. Twenty-six patients with a positive ultrasound and without a biopsy underwent sonographic surveillance, 20 patients had unchanged findings, and 5 had decreased/resolved findings. Conclusion The prevalence of malignant pediatric breast masses is exceedingly low. No malignant breast masses were found in our cohort; however, diagnosis should be suspected based on the clinical presentation and ultrasound appearance. The low percentage of malignant breast masses suggests sonographic surveillance and patient education are feasible and safe management approaches in most adolescent breast mass cases. Advances in knowledge This study provides 1 of the largest analyses of adolescent breast ultrasounds, showing that malignancy is exceedingly rare and supporting sonographic surveillance as a safe management approach.

title: Airway imaging practices in primary ciliary dyskinesia: a global survey to guide standardized guidelines.
abstract: Objectives Airway imaging guidelines for primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) are currently limited. Given the progressive nature of this disease, standardized imaging protocols, particularly at key clinical milestones such as diagnosis, routine reviews, and exacerbations, may improve monitoring of disease progression, support comparison of outcomes across centers, and provide robust parameters for clinical trials. Methods To document current practices, we conducted a global survey of PCD clinicians. An online questionnaire was distributed via international PCD networks, covering imaging use at diagnosis, during routine assessments, and at exacerbations treated with oral or intravenous antibiotics. Responses were received from 120 clinicians across 90 centers in 33 countries. Modalities assessed included X-ray, CT scans, MRI, and ultrasound, with analyses stratified by center type and size. Results At diagnosis, 94% of clinicians reported using imaging. Chest X-ray was most common for children under 5 years (55%), whereas CT was preferred for older patients (66%). During routine assessments, 67.5% of clinicians used imaging, but timing and modality varied, with CT more frequent in pediatric and mixed centers. Imaging during exacerbations differed by treatment route: chest X-ray was the most common modality, used by 57.1% for oral antibiotic-treated episodes and 73.3% for intravenous episodes. CT use was higher with intravenous treatment (15.8% vs. 4.2%). Conclusions Although practices varied, consistent trends at diagnosis and follow-up highlight opportunities for consensus. Advances in knowledge Standardized imaging protocols could enhance clinical care, enable meaningful research comparisons, and improve outcomes in PCD.

title: Ensuring radiology reporting quality across a national lung cancer screening program.
abstract: Low-dose CT (LDCT) for lung cancer screening (LCS) in high-risk individuals reduces both lung cancer-specific and all-cause mortality, supported by data from the National Lung Screening Trial, NELSON, the International Early Lung Cancer Action Program (I-ELCAP). In 2019, following a successful pilot, the UK National Health Service announced rollout of the Targeted Lung Health Check (TLHC) program, offering ever-smokers aged 55-74 an appointment with a health professional, which may lead to referral for LDCT based on individual risk of developing lung cancer assessed using validated multivariable risk-prediction models (PLCOm2012 and the Liverpool Lung Project model, LLPv2). As LCS expands, it is paramount that radiologists who participate in screening are adequately qualified and properly trained. To ensure the radiology reporting for an expanding program remains clinically and cost effective, reporters must engage with nationally-set quality assurance (QA) policies. In this article, we describe the approach taken by The HLH Imaging Group (HLH), a provider reporting ∼85% of LCS scans in NHS England (NHSE), to embed near real-time and routine double-read QA alongside the national external quality assurance (EQA) scheme (PERFECTS). We present aggregate referral-rate data from reporters in our network across the 2025-26 financial year and compare current NHSE fixed thresholds, with statistically-derived thresholds (mean ± 2SD; median ± k·MAD). We provide explicit rationale for our operational choices (a 2-consecutive-quarter outlier definition, 25-case retrospective review of flagged reporters, and 5% random sampling of negative reports for blinded double reading). We explicitly acknowledge that this describes a provider's approach within a wider radiological workforce; PERFECTS remains the only program-wide QA covering all NHSE LCS readers. We propose that the elements described could form the basis of an NHSE/Department of Health and Social Care standardized near real-time QA framework applicable across all LCS providers.

title: Use of whole-body MRI to evaluate residual tumor burden after initial systemic therapy in polymetastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.
abstract: Objectives Treatment options for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) have expanded, with evidence supporting prostate radiotherapy in low-volume disease. However, evidence for consolidative radiotherapy to residual sites in patients rendered oligometastatic after systemic therapy is lacking. Advanced imaging with WB-MRI and PSMA PET/CT enables more accurate assessment of tumor burden and response. Methods This feasibility study assessed response to initial systemic treatment with an ARPI or docetaxel in 29 patients with polymetastatic (>5 metastases) HSPC. PSA and WB-MRI response using MET-RADS-P criteria were recorded. Results A total of 20/29 (69.0.%) of patients were down-risked to oligometastatic disease (≤5 sites) after a median of 5.5 (IQR 5-5.8) months, identified on WB-MRI. Median PSA was 0.2 ng/mL (IQR 0.1-0.7) in down-risked patients vs 1.5 ng/mL (IQR 1.1-84) in those not down-risked. Residual intraprostatic disease was seen in 55% (11/20) of down-risked patients. Conclusions Most patients were down-risked on WB-MRI, supporting the existence of an induced oligometastatic state and providing rationale for the STAR TRAP randomized trial (ISRCTN16448082), which will assess the role of consolidative radiotherapy in this setting. Advances in knowledge WB-MRI correlates with PSA response and shows potential as an imaging biomarker in mHSPC in this small feasibility study.

title: CT low attenuation area quantification versus visual scoring for early pulmonary emphysema detection in lung cancer screening.
abstract: Objectives To compare low-attenuation analysis (LAA) with visual scoring and explore their application in the detection of emphysema in low-dose CT (LDCT) scans. Methods A random cohort of 352 CT examinations from health-check participants was selected from a lung cancer screening(LCS) dataset. Scans were evaluated for emphysema by four readers according to latest Fleischner criteria, and emphysema was quantified by LAA with thresholds from -900 HU to -980 HU. Fleiss' Kappa assessed inter-reader agreement on visual detection and severity classification. Cases with full agreement on emphysema presence were used to compare LAA quantification and visual detection. Spearman correlation test measured their correlation and Cohen's Kappa evaluated the agreement between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection. Results Agreement among four observers was found in 266 cases on emphysema presence based on visual evaluation (K = 0.738, 0.737-0.739). Concordance between emphysema presence using a LAA% cutoff of 6% and binary visual classification was 61.3% (163/266, Cohen's Kappa:0.173. Spearman analysis showed a correlation between LAA% and visual scores (P < 0.05). Conclusions LAA emphysema quantification shows in comparison with visual scoring limited performance for discrimination of normal and emphysematous lung parenchyma in a Low dose CT Lung cancer screening dataset. Advances in knowledge Full agreement among four readers regarding visual emphysema classification was achieved in only three-quarters of cases. Limited concordance was found between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection.

title: Deep learning multimodal fusion model based on ultrasound images and clinical-ultrasound texts for differentiating benign and malignant renal tumors.
abstract: To develop a deep learning multimodal fusion model based on ultrasound (US) images and clinical-US texts to differentiate benign and malignant renal tumors. The retrospective dataset from January 2012 to February 2023 in a tertiary hospital was used for model development and randomly allocated to training and validation sets. An independent prospective test set was obtained from March 2023 to October 2024. We developed Model-G using grayscale US (GUS) images, Model-GC using GUS and color Doppler flow imaging images, Model-T using clinical-US texts, and Model-UT using US images and clinical-US texts. ResNet50 was used for image feature extraction, BERT for text encoding, and ViT for multimodal classification. In total, 1008 patients (740 in training set, 186 validation set, and 82 prospective test set) with a single renal tumor were included. In the validation set, Model-UT achieved the highest diagnostic performance in comparison to Model-G, Model-GC, and Model-T with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.89 (95% CI, 0.86-0.93) (all p-values < 0.05). In the prospective test set, Model-UT yielded an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86-0.97), outperforming high-level, mid-level, and low-level radiologists (all p-values < 0.05). The multimodal fusion model presents promising potential in differentiating benign and malignant renal tumors. Deep learning model integrating US images with clinical-US texts improved benign-versus-malignant renal tumor differentiation. Decision-curve, controlled ablation, and SHAP analyses support its potential use as a clinical decision-support tool.

title: The Importance of Molecular Imaging Response Criteria: Rationale and Overview.
abstract: Assessment of therapeutic response in oncology is fundamental for evaluating treatment efficacy, guiding clinical decision-making, and determining prognosis. Historically, response evaluation relied primarily on anatomical imaging criteria derived from tumor size changes on computed tomography (CT), most notably the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) and its adaptations. However, advances in molecular imaging, particularly positron emission tomography (PET) using [18F]-2-fluoro-2-deoxyglucose ([18F]FDG) and other radiopharmaceuticals, have introduced new biomarkers capable of detecting tumor response earlier than structural changes. Molecular imaging-based criteria, including EORTC, PERCIST, immune-adapted PET frameworks, and disease-specific systems such as Lugano, RANO, ENETS SSTR-PeRForm and RECIP, provide quantitative assessment of tumor burden and may better reflect biologic response to therapy. This review discusses the rationale behind molecular imaging response criteria, outlines the principles of CT-based and PET-based evaluation systems, and highlights the clinical relevance of integrating metabolic imaging into tumor response.

title: Long-term outcomes of indeterminate breast (B3) lesions managed with vacuum-assisted excision.
abstract: Background UK guidelines for indeterminate (B3) breast lesions recommend vacuum-assisted excision (VAE) over diagnostic surgery. However, there is little long-term follow-up published post VAE management. This study evaluates immediate and long-term outcomes of women with B3 lesions managed predominantly through radiological pathways. Methods Single-centre retrospective review of B3 lesions diagnosed between October 2011 and August 2017, evaluating outcomes following immediate management and subsequent breast cancer development during follow-up until February 2022. Results 513 women (median age 53yrs) were diagnosed with B3 lesions between October 2011 and August 2017. 391 (76.2%) had radiological management with second-line VAE, 48 (9.4%) had diagnostic excision and 74 (14.4%) had no second-line procedure. 54 lesions (10.5%) were upgraded to malignancy. Yearly mammography (atypia lesions, 5yrs) or three-yearly screening (non-atypia lesions) was offered to the remaining 459 women. 44/459 (9.6%) women had no mammographic follow-up (patient decision).Breast cancer occurred in 33 patients (7.2%), the majority (23/33, 69.7%) detected during imaging surveillance. 10 cancers (30.3%) occurred at the original B3 site. 5-year cumulative incidence of breast cancer was 6.3% (95% CI: 3.9%-8.7%). No significant difference in 5-year cumulative incidence of breast cancer between women with atypia (7.8%; 95% CI 4.3-11.2%) or without atypia (4.3%; 95% CI 1.1-7.4%) was demonstrated (p = 0.375). Conclusions Radiological management of B3 lesions is safe and effective. Following initial management, women with B3 lesions have a small risk of subsequent breast cancer, similar for lesions with or without atypia, most of which could be safely managed within normal screening pathways. Advances in knowledge Vacuum-assisted excision can safely and effectively manage appropriate indeterminate breast lesionsRisk of breast cancer following B3 diagnosis is lowNo statistically significant difference in subsequent breast cancer risk was demonstrated between B3 lesions with and without atypia.

title: Parameter analysis for diffusion tensor imaging corresponding to microstructural alterations following spinal cord injury.
abstract: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) is a quantitative MRI technique that enables non-invasive, in vivo evaluation of spinal cord injury (SCI). Based on the anisotropy of water molecule diffusion, DTI provides superior detection of microstructural alterations compared with conventional MRI. Diffusion is quantified by parameters including fractional anisotropy (FA), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), average diffusion coefficient (DCavg), axial diffusion (AD), radial diffusion (RD), and mean diffusion (MD), each showing distinct temporal sensitivity to SCI. Changes in these indices reflect underlying tissue disruption and are closely correlated with neurological function in both experimental and clinical studies. Despite extensive investigations, a systematic summary of their diagnostic and prognostic value has been lacking. This review highlights parameter sensitivity at different injury stages and the associated microstructural changes. AD and DCavg demonstrated high sensitivity in the acute phase, whereas FA was particularly sensitive in the chronic phase. ADC and MD showed mild sensitivity in acute and subacute stages but became more relevant chronically, while RD exhibited low sensitivity in acute phase but progressively increased over time. Collectively, DTI provides critical diagnostic information, and cross-linked analysis of multiple metrics across time points enables more accurate evaluation of SCI severity and prognosis.

title: Retrospective multi-reader evaluation of a Deep-Learning-based cancer detection model in Contrast-Enhanced Mammography.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the clinical impact of a deep-learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool applied to contrast-enhanced mammography on radiologists' diagnostic accuracy and reading efficiency. Methods In this retrospective single-centre study, 150 contrast-enhanced mammography examinations were interpreted by five radiologists. Each case was read and annotated twice in two sequential sessions: first without assistance and then with the computer-aided diagnostic tool, with a minimum 4-week washout period. Diagnostic performance was assessed at lesion and breast levels using free-response receiver operating characteristic analysis, area under the curve, and false-positive rate. Reading time for one radiologist was recorded as an exploratory measure. Results The computer-aided diagnostic tool was associated with improved lesion-level performance for most radiologists, with a mean increase in the area under the free-response curve of 0.030 ± 0.018. At 89% sensitivity, false-positive findings decreased by an average of 11.4% ± 24% across all radiologists. No improvement was observed at the breast level, possibly related to the tool's single-view analysis and dataset characteristics. An exploratory analysis showed a 31% reduction in reading time for one radiologist. Conclusion Integration of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool into contrast-enhanced mammography was associated with improved lesion-level diagnostic performance and reduced false-positive findings, without measurable improvement at the breast level. Advances in knowledge To our knowledge, this study provides one of the early clinical evaluations of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool for contrast-enhanced mammography, suggesting potential improvements in lesion-level diagnostic performance and workflow efficiency while highlighting current limitations at the breast level.

title: A transparent gel pad bolus enabling direct skin recognition in surface-guided radiation therapy.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the feasibility of repurposing a transparent ultrasound gel pad as a radiotherapy bolus, we focused on dosimetric performance and compatibility with surface-guided radiation therapy (SGRT). Methods A gel pad bolus composed of tamarind seed gum and polyhydric alcohols was compared with a conventional gel bolus and a thermoplastic bolus. Percent depth dose was measured for 6 MV and 10 MV photon beams and 6 MeV and 9 MeV electron beams. Straight-line optical transmittance was assessed over 380-830 nm. Surface recognition accuracy was quantified using the AlignRT SGRT system on a breast phantom. Results The gel pad produced a measurable bolus effect for both photon and electron beams, although superficial dose enhancement was lower than that of conventional materials (85.5% vs 90.3-91.5% at 6 MV). Deep doses beyond dmax agreed within 1% for photon beams. At 730 nm, the gel pad bolus demonstrated high transmittance (92.3%), compared with the gel (19.8%) and HM (36.6%) boluses. The SGRT recognition rate with the gel pad bolus (89.10%) was comparable to the no-bolus condition (92.93%, p = 0.13), whereas conventional boluses significantly reduced recognition (p < 0.001). Conclusions The transparent gel pad bolus enabled direct SGRT-based recognition of the underlying skin surface while maintaining clinically relevant bolus functionality. Advances in knowledge Optical transparency enables SGRT monitoring through a bolus, highlighting optical compatibility as an important design consideration.

title: Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of Image-Guided Aspiration Techniques for Periprosthetic Hip Infection: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Objectives Image-guided fluid aspiration is a key component in the diagnostic work-up of suspected prosthetic joint infection of the hip (PJI). Fluoroscopy, ultrasound (US), and computed tomography (CT) are frequently employed to guide aspiration; however, comparative evidence regarding their diagnostic performance and procedural outcomes remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the diagnostic accuracy and technical performance of these modalities. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL were searched for studies evaluating fluoroscopy-, US-, or CT-guided hip aspiration to aid PJI diagnosis. Outcomes of interest included diagnostic performance, dry tap rates, and procedural characteristics. Dry tap rates were pooled by modality using random-effects meta-analysis of proportions. Due to heterogeneity in reference standards, diagnostic accuracy outcomes were synthesised narratively. Results Ten studies comprising 1,574 hip aspirations were included (647 fluoroscopy, 831 US, 96 CT). Sensitivity ranged from 0.52-0.89 for US and 0.27-0.83 for fluoroscopy, with consistently high specificity (≥0.75) across modalities. CT-guided aspiration demonstrated sensitivity of 0.67 and specificity of 0.98 in a single study. Pooled dry tap rates were lower for US (17%, 95% CI 4-30%) compared with fluoroscopy (27%, 95% CI 9-45%), with substantial heterogeneity (I²>97%). Conclusions Reported specificity is comparable between ultrasound- and fluoroscopy-guided hip aspiration for PJI. Ultrasound-guided aspiration demonstrates higher reported sensitivity and lower dry tap rates, although interpretation is limited by heterogeneity in reference standards. Advances in knowledge This review provides a focused synthesis of comparative evidence on imaging modalities for hip aspiration in PJI. It highlights a potential diagnostic and practical advantage of ultrasound-guided aspiration.

title: Tibial bone stress injury-a common cause of leg pain in sports.
abstract: Introduction Tibial bone stress injuries (TBSI), encompassing tibial stress fractures (TSF) and medial tibial stress syndrome (MTSS), represent a significant spectrum of overuse pathology in active individuals, accounting for 22%-46% of sports-related stress injuries. These conditions feature distinct pathophysiological mechanisms and management pathways requiring precise diagnostic differentiation. Sources of data Narrative review of primary and secondary literature sourced from PubMed and relevant clinical databases. Areas of agreement Both conditions result from repetitive tibial loading without adequate rest and share overlapping risk factors. Management is primarily non-operative, with activity modification followed by graded rehabilitation. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the definitive imaging modality for TSF and is valuable in excluding differential diagnoses in MTSS. Areas of controversy The utility of the Fredericson MRI grading system is debated. Certain intermediate grades may be clinically indistinguishable, and its prognostic value in paediatric populations is questioned. Furthermore, heterogeneous nomenclature used interchangeably impedes clear clinical communication. Growing points Whether MTSS and TSF represent a shared pathological continuum or distinct clinical entities with overlapping risk factors remains unresolved, with histological evidence suggesting divergent pathophysiological mechanisms. Multicentre validation of MRI grading against functional outcomes and longitudinal studies evaluating early biomechanical interventions are key research priorities. Areas timely for developing research Generalizability of evidence is limited by homogenous study populations and the absence of a universal return-to-sport definition. Priority must be given to establishing multidisciplinary consensus on nomenclature, diagnostic imaging thresholds, and risk-stratified rehabilitation protocols tailored to injury severity and comorbidities.
originalAbstract:
Introduction

Tibial bone stress injuries (TBSI), encompassing tibial stress fractures (TSF) and medial tibial stress syndrome (MTSS), represent a significant spectrum of overuse pathology in active individuals, accounting for 22%-46% of sports-related stress injuries. These conditions feature distinct pathophysiological mechanisms and management pathways requiring precise diagnostic differentiation.

Sources of data

Narrative review of primary and secondary literature sourced from PubMed and relevant clinical databases.

Areas of agreement

Both conditions result from repetitive tibial loading without adequate rest and share overlapping risk factors. Management is primarily non-operative, with activity modification followed by graded rehabilitation. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the definitive imaging modality for TSF and is valuable in excluding differential diagnoses in MTSS.

Areas of controversy

The utility of the Fredericson MRI grading system is debated. Certain intermediate grades may be clinically indistinguishable, and its prognostic value in paediatric populations is questioned. Furthermore, heterogeneous nomenclature used interchangeably impedes clear clinical communication.

Growing points

Whether MTSS and TSF represent a shared pathological continuum or distinct clinical entities with overlapping risk factors remains unresolved, with histological evidence suggesting divergent pathophysiological mechanisms. Multicentre validation of MRI grading against functional outcomes and longitudinal studies evaluating early biomechanical interventions are key research priorities.

Areas timely for developing research

Generalizability of evidence is limited by homogenous study populations and the absence of a universal return-to-sport definition. Priority must be given to establishing multidisciplinary consensus on nomenclature, diagnostic imaging thresholds, and risk-stratified rehabilitation protocols tailored to injury severity and comorbidities.

title: White matter hyperintensity burden in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: motor and survival correlates.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive motor neuron degeneration. Microvascular dysfunction has been implicated by recent research in ALS pathogenesis and motor neuron vulnerability. The aim of this study is to investigate whether MRI markers of white matter hyperintensities (WMHs), reflecting small-vessel disease, are associated with motor and cognitive impairment, disease staging and prognosis in ALS. In this retrospective cohort study MRI scans from 399 ALS patients were evaluated for periventricular and deep white matter hyperintensities (pvWMH and dWMH) using visual grading scales together with semi-automated volumetric quantification of relative WMH volume (WMHrv). The primary outcome was survival. Secondary outcomes included disease staging, functional impairment, motor and cognitive outcome measures. WMH burden was associated with more advanced King's topographic staging [pvWMH (P < 0.001), dWMH (P = 0.002)] and MiToS functional staging [pvWMH (P < 0.001), dWMH (P = 0.017)]. High pvWMH burden was associated with shorter survival [exp(β) = 3.503; 95% CI = 1.131, 10.832; P = 0.030] after adjustment for known prognostic factors. WMH measures correlated with greater functional impairment on ALSFRS-R score [pvWMH (P < 0.001), dWMH (P = 0.003), WMHrv (P = 0.008)]. WMH burden correlated with more severe lower, but not upper, motor neuron impairment, as measured with the MRC sum score [pvWMH (P = 0.002), dWMH (P = 0.024), WMHrv (p=0.030)] and lower motor neuron score [pvWMH (P < 0.001), dWMH (P = 0.001)]. WMH burden was also associated with cognitive deficits on the Edinburgh Cognitive and Behavioural ALS Screen (ECAS), as indicated by total [pvWMH (P = 0.007), dWMH (P = 0.009), WMHrv (P = 0.037)] and ALS-specific ECAS scores [pvWMH (P = 0.001), dWMH (P = 0.020), WMHrv (P = 0.022)]. This large-scale MRI study links small-vessel disease to clinical staging, survival and ALS-specific motor (distinctively LMN) and cognitive impairments. These results suggest that WMHs may reflect a diffuse neurovascular pathology spanning cortical and spinal regions and may be relevant to ALS progression. Routine MRI assessment of WMHs could aid patient stratification and inform trial designs. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify causal relationships and neurovascular-targeted therapeutic implications.

title: Regional blood-brain barrier dysfunction maps to lower performance in cognitive ageing.
abstract: Age-related cognitive decline is a common and growing public health challenge, associated with loss of independence, reduced quality of life, increased caregiver burden and substantial healthcare and societal costs. Yet cognitive decline in ageing is heterogeneous, and current clinical constructs do not reliably capture the underlying biological mechanisms or predict progression to dementia. This cross-sectional study examined whether blood-brain barrier dysfunction (BBBD) provides a biologically supported correlate of cognitive performance beyond clinical diagnosis. The study included 46 patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), 46 age-matched controls and 43 young controls. BBBD was assessed using dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI in 42 patients with MCI and all controls, alongside volumetric brain analysis. Standardized NeuroTrax cognitive assessment data were analysed for 41 MCI patients and 19 age-matched controls. BBBD was analysed using the BBBdetect software (Emagix Inc, Nova Scotia, Canada), quantifying voxelwise and region-wise blood-brain barrier permeability; volumetric analysis was performed using the Volbrain software; and cognitive performance was stratified into low- and high-performance subgroups based on modified z-scores. Compared with young controls, the older cohort (MCI patients combined with age-matched controls) showed significantly greater BBBD volume and regional extent. Permeability increased with age and showed marked inter-individual variability. Across participants, lower cognitive performance was associated with a greater number of regions exhibiting BBBD. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified domain-specific spatial patterns of BBBD linked to poor performance in memory, executive, attention, verbal and motor domains, implicating frontal, cingulate, hippocampal, basal ganglia and cerebellar regions. In contrast, volumetric analyses revealed expected age-related reductions in grey and white matter and cortical thickness along with increased ventricular volume; however, these structural changes showed weak to no associations with cognitive performance. These findings suggest that BBBD is widespread in ageing and that regional BBBD maps to domain-specific cognitive deficits. BBBD thus emerges as a biologically relevant biomarker of age-related cognitive impairment and a potential therapeutic target for preserving cognitive function in ageing.

title: Metabolic connectivity and memory in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy.
abstract: Memory decline after anterior mesial temporal resection in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (MTLE-HS) remains incompletely explained by structural and clinical factors, suggesting that networks may contribute to cognitive vulnerability. We investigated whether presurgical metabolic connectivity (MC), derived from fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and reflecting metabolic network organization, is associated with memory performance and postsurgical cognitive outcome in MTLE-HS. We studied 83 patients with MTLE-HS who underwent anterior mesial temporal resection. All had interictal FDG-PET and pre- and postsurgical neuropsychological testing. MC was computed using a normative connectivity framework and examined in relation to memory performance, analysed separately for left and right TLE. The effect of resection extent on cognitive outcome was also assessed. Presurgical analyses revealed distinct lateralized patterns. In right temporal lobe epilepsy (RTLE), immediate visual memory correlated positively with MC across widespread fronto-cingulate-temporal networks, frequently including the lesional hippocampus. In left temporal lobe epilepsy (LTLE), immediate verbal memory showed only negative correlations with extratemporal MC. In RTLE, presurgical MC also correlated with postsurgical change in immediate visual memory. Predominantly negative associations involved ipsilateral hippocampal-cingulate and fronto-temporal pathways, whereas positive correlations were confined to contralateral posterior cingulate connections with frontal and temporal regions. In LTLE, no significant correlations with postsurgical memory change were identified. Extent of resection did not correlate with cognitive outcome. MC was significantly associated with memory performance in MTLE-HS, showing clear lateralized differences. In RTLE, presurgical MC was associated with postsurgical outcome: ipsilateral hippocampal-cingulate connectivity was linked to decline, whereas contralateral posterior cingulate pathways supported preservation. No such associations were found in LTLE, consistent with more constrained network reorganization within left-lateralized verbal memory systems. These effects were independent of resection extent, indicating that memory prognosis after AMTR in RTLE may depend on network-level mechanisms and that FDG-PET-derived MC could serve as a biomarker for cognitive risk assessment.

title: Tegmental atrophy in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder: ex vivo MRI-informed in vivo imaging.
abstract: Isolated rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) is an early-stage synucleinopathy characterized by brainstem pathology. In rodents, the pontine tegmentum contains a REM sleep centre, the sublaterodorsal nucleus, which expresses corticotropin-releasing hormone binding protein (CRHBP). While the involvement of brainstem pathophysiology is thus implicated in iRBD, its solid evidence remains scarce in humans due to the difficulty in identifying small brainstem nuclei with conventional MRI technology alone. Here, we aimed to detect tegmental atrophy in iRBD with voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis combined with a novel human brainstem atlas. Structural MRIs from 98 patients with iRBD and 114 controls were analysed to investigate grey matter volume using VBM. Our unique approach involved detailed assessments of the VBM results, guided by a high-resolution MRI-based atlas of the human brainstem. This brainstem atlas was founded on ex vivo MRI of 10 post-mortem human specimens. We validated it with CRHBP immunostaining, which aided in identifying putative REM sleep-regulating nuclei in humans. We applied this brainstem atlas to identify atrophy in specific brainstem regions in iRBD and correlate their volumes with clinical and polysomnographic measures. Voxel-based morphometry revealed a focal cluster of grey matter atrophy in the dorsal pontine tegmentum of iRBD patients, including the laterodorsal tegmental nucleus, ventral part (LDTgV) and the pedunculopontine tegmental nucleus (PTg). Our atlas-based analysis confirmed the LDTgV as the site of most conspicuous atrophy, revealing a significant volume reduction in iRBD patients compared with controls with a moderate effect size (Cohen's d = 0.44, Bonferroni-corrected P = 0.019). Furthermore, greater atrophy in the LDTgV and the PTg was associated with more severe autonomic dysfunction as measured by Scales for Outcomes in Parkinson's Disease-Autonomic dysfunction scores (partial r = -0.237, P = 0.021 and partial r = -0.236, P = 0.021, respectively). In 23 patients from whom quantitative polysomnographic data were available, LDTgV atrophy was correlated with the percentage ratio of REM sleep without atonia (partial r = -0.491, P = 0.028). Histological analysis confirmed that the LDTgV is selectively enriched with CRHBP-positive neurons, a putative marker for REM sleep-on neurons. We provided novel evidence for the involvement of LDTgV, the putative human homologue of the murine sublaterodorsal nucleus, in iRBD. The present findings advance our understanding of the neuroanatomical basis of iRBD and will contribute to the development of early biomarkers for α-synucleinopathies.

title: Cerebellar involvement in sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: a magnetic resonance spectroscopy study.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is increasingly recognized as a multisystem neurodegenerative disorder, and recent evidence suggests that the cerebellum may contribute to disease pathology, although cerebellar metabolic alterations have not previously been demonstrated in vivo. This study investigated cerebellar metabolic and structural changes using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) and volumetric imaging. Thirty patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (21 M, mean age 59.7 ± 7.6 years), 22 healthy controls (HC, 10 M, mean age 59.8 ± 9.6 years) and 16 individuals with hereditary spastic paraplegia type 4 (8 M, mean age 50.8 ± 12.5 years), a potential clinical mimic, underwent 3T MRI and 1H-MRS with a single-voxel positioned in the left cerebellar hemisphere. Patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis showed significant reductions in myo-inositol/creatinine (P = 0.01) and glutathione/creatinine (P = 0.005), compared with HC, together with selective volume loss in cerebellar lobules I-IV, V, VI, and Crus I. Among metabolites, glutathione/creatinine had the highest discriminative accuracy for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis versus both HC and spastic paraplegia type 4, with areas under the curve of 0.80 and 0.71, respectively. These findings reveal distinct cerebellar metabolic alterations in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, providing further evidence for cerebellar involvement in disease pathology and highlighting cerebellar 1H-MRS as a potential adjunct to diagnostic evaluation.
