title: Documented Fracture-Healing Outcomes After Operative and Nonoperative Management of Closed Mid-Diaphyseal Humerus Fractures in Active-Duty Service Members.
abstract: Introduction Closed diaphyseal humerus fracture treatment is nuanced with regard to the selection of surgical candidates. Fracture union is crucial, with historical data suggesting rivaling union rates between operative and nonoperative treatment; however, recent literature suggests increased union rates with operative treatment. Although nonoperative treatment of most fracture patterns is supported by the literature, there remains an argument for operative treatment for select patient populations, especially when considering union rates. Evidence regarding fracture-healing outcomes in young active-duty populations remains limited. We sought to characterize documented fracture-healing outcomes after operative and nonoperative management of closed diaphyseal humerus fractures in active-duty service members and to evaluate completeness of healing-status ascertainment. Methods This study queried the Medical Assessment and Readiness System (MARS), Womack Army Medical Center, Fort Bragg, NC, which contains information from the Military Health System (MHS) care system. This study defined a retrospective cohort of patients diagnosed with closed diaphyseal humerus fractures (OTA/AO 12A/B/C), using International Classification of Diseases (9th and 10th revision) codes, sustained from January 2011 to December 2022. Treatment type, including operative or nonoperative, was identified. We excluded patients with open humerus fractures; proximal humerus fractures; distal humerus fractures; and those treated with external fixation. The primary outcome measure was a diagnosis of union or malunion/nonunion. Unadjusted comparisons between groups were conducted using likelihood ratio chi-square tests. Results The study population comprised 402 patients with closed humeral diaphyseal fractures; 314 (78.1%) were managed nonoperatively and 88 (21.9%) operatively. Fracture-healing status could be classified in 216 patients (53.7%), whereas 186 (46.3%) lacked sufficient documentation to determine the primary outcome. Outcome ascertainment was more complete after operative than nonoperative management (61/88 [69.3%] vs. 155/314 [49.4%]; P = .001). Among those with documented healing status, union occurred in 149 of 155 nonoperatively managed fractures (96.1%; 95% CI, 91.8%-98.6%) and 59 of 61 operatively managed fractures (96.7%; 95% CI, 88.7%-99.6%). Discussion Among active-duty service members with documented healing status after closed diaphyseal humerus fracture, observed union rates were high after both nonoperative and operative management. However, treatment was nonrandom, important fracture-specific treatment-selection variables were unavailable, and healing status was determined from available clinical documentation, recorded radiographic interpretations, diagnosis codes, and revision procedures rather than standardized radiographic adjudication. These limitations, together with incomplete and differential outcome ascertainment and few nonunion/malunion events, preclude estimation of a comparative treatment effect. The findings should therefore be interpreted descriptively rather than as evidence of equivalence between operative and nonoperative treatment.

title: The Ongoing Utility of Historical Military Photofluorographs-Tools to Identify Fallen US Soldiers From Past Wars as Cross-Validated by DNA and Dental Data in 180 Cases.
abstract: Introduction Mass chest X-ray formed a routine part of induction processes to the US armed forces in the 1940-1950s for tuberculosis screening. Today, the skeletal structure recorded in these medical miniature films serves to identify these same soldiers. In the US military's accounting/repatriation setting, chest radiograph comparisons have grown to be a primary identification mechanism alongside DNA and dental records. Identifications are now routinely conducted with contributions from miniature radiographic films. This article reviews the miniature radiographic film as an identification tool and provides the first evaluation of findings (180 cases) against gold standards of DNA and dental analyses for the very same cases. Materials and methods This article reviews both miniature film photofluorographs and the standardized chest radiograph comparison (CXR) protocol employed by the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA) for identification. Additionally, all DPAA cases (2010-2025) where radiographic CXR resulted in a match result (280) were reviewed for additional DNA and/or dental record findings, providing 180 cases where dual-modality result existed to cross-validation test the radiographic analyses. Results For 172 DNA cases, there was no instance of disagreement between the chest radiograph result and the independently acquired Armed Forces DNA Identification Laboratory's DNA result. For 8 dental cases reporting a positive match result, the CXR identity finding was identical (both evidence lines identified the same person). To be conservative, we assume that the next future CXR case to be conducted using miniature films will yield an erroneous result, thereby setting a positive predictive value for radiographic comparison of 99.4% (=180 correct results/181 total decisions). Conclusions Miniature chest radiographs provide useful identification-relevant information. DPAA casework provides a rare circumstance to evaluate the accuracy of miniature film radiograph comparisons across a large sample, as multiple independent and parallel lines of analysis exist for single cases. Evaluation of these cases (180 in total) reveals that the military miniature films supply the same name associations that DNA and forensic odontology provide. The positive predictive value is high (99.4%), conservatively assuming the next case to be an incorrect one. This confirms the value of the miniature chest film and CXR methods, when DNA and dental records alone are unable to provide definitive answers.

title: IgG4-related kidney disease: treatment standard.
abstract: IgG4-related disease is a systemic, immune-mediated, fibro-inflammatory condition that can affect virtually any organ. IgG4-related kidney disease represents one of the most clinically relevant manifestations and encompasses a spectrum of renal manifestations, including IgG4-related tubulointerstitial nephritis, membranous nephropathy, and obstructive uropathy secondary to retroperitoneal fibrosis. The diagnosis remains challenging and requires integration of clinical and laboratory findings, along with imaging, and histopathology, as no single biomarker is sufficiently sensitive or specific. Although systemic immunosuppressive therapies largely overlap across manifestations, the practical management differs substantially between parenchymal kidney disease and retroperitoneal fibrosis, particularly with regard to mechanisms of kidney injury, the need for interventional procedures, treatment goals, and monitoring strategies. Glucocorticoids are the cornerstone of induction therapy and typically provide rapid clinical responses; however, the chronic-relapsing course of IgG4-related disease and the burden of glucocorticoid-related toxicity have prompted investigation in steroid-sparing strategies. Conventional immunosuppressive agents have been used with controversial results, whereas B-cell-targeting therapies, particularly rituximab, have demonstrated high efficacy in both induction and maintenance settings. Management should ultimately be individualised, taking into account the pattern of renal involvement, organ dysfunction, and likelihood of reversibility. In patients with obstructive uropathy due to retroperitoneal fibrosis, interventional procedures may be required alongside immunosuppressive therapy. Long-term monitoring is essential because of the relapsing nature of the disease and the potential for chronic kidney disease. This Treatment Standard provides a practical, nephrology-oriented framework for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of IgG4-related kidney disease, integrating current evidence with emerging insights from immunopathogenesis and clinical trials.

title: An evidence-based workflow for integrating molecular testing with histopathology in the workup of meningiomas.
abstract: Background Meningiomas are graded using histologic and molecular criteria according to the World Health Organization (WHO) classification. However, there is scant evidence considering the specific value of each individual atypical histological feature that contributes to WHO grading. There is also little evidence-based guidance as to which cases should receive molecular testing. Methods Detailed histological information was collected for 1058 resected meningiomas, including cases with genomic DNA methylation and copy number variant (CNV) data, next-generation sequencing, and RNA risk score. Integrated analyses were conducted using known prognostic variables, including WHO Grade, Ki-67, mitotic index (MI), and atypical histologic features (necrosis, hypercellularity, macronucleoli, sheeting, and small cells). Results Necrosis, elevated MI, and increased WHO grade correlated with specific DNA methylation patterns, RNA risk groups, and chromosomal CNVs. Predictive analysis identified MI as the strongest single correlate, and suggested the presence of ≥ 2 atypical features as an optimal threshold for recurrence prediction. Sheeting architecture was the only independent histologic correlate of recurrence. Integration of histologic and molecular features suggests that tumors with high MI have poor prognosis regardless of molecular profile. Further analysis of low MI tumors revealed specific predictors of unfavorable molecular profiles. Conclusions These data indicate that some atypical histopathologic features are more powerful than others, and can be used on initial screening to increase the yield of molecular profiling of meningiomas. Furthermore, we propose that molecular testing may actually have greatest added value in cases with low, not high, MI.

title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: An Overarching Review.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across neuro-oncology domains to analyze complex, high-dimensional, multimodal data. Despite major advances in the biological understanding and classification of CNS tumors, clinical outcomes for many of them remain poor, reflecting intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneity and limitations of conventional reductionist approaches. AI offers a paradigm shift to capture this heterogeneity and provide quantitative, reproducible diagnostic, predictive, and prognostic insights. This article describes a joint effort across the Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) working groups to provide an overarching review of the AI use across six key domains of neuro-oncology: neuroimaging, neuropathology, laboratory medicine, neurosurgery, drug discovery, and clinical trials. Applications closest to clinical use include imaging segmentation and quantification, AI-assisted image reconstruction, DNA methylation-based classification, and workflow optimization. Radiogenomics, WSI-based molecular prediction, AI-guided surgical targeting, liquid biopsy interpretation, AI-guided drug discovery, digital twins, and in silico trials remain promising but require stronger prospective validation. Key challenges include limited availability of large diverse datasets, variability in data acquisition and reference standards, and limited external validation. This review provides a unifying framework for understanding the role of AI across neuro-oncology and highlights key considerations for its responsible implementation, emphasizing standardization, reproducibility, multi-institutional validation, and human oversight.

title: MRI-Based Machine Learning to Differentiate True Progression from Pseudoprogression in Glioblastoma: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Differentiating true progression (TP) from pseudoprogression (PsP) after chemoradiation for glioblastoma remains clinically difficult. We evaluated externally validated diagnostic performance of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based machine learning models and appraised study quality and transparency. Methods PubMed, Embase, MEDLINE, and Cochrane Library were searched through October 1, 2025 (PROSPERO registration CRD420251144894). Eligible adult glioblastoma studies used MRI-based machine learning to distinguish TP from PsP against histopathology and/or clinicoradiologic follow-up. The primary meta-analysis included external test cohorts with extractable 2 × 2 data; internal and combined internal and external test analyses were secondary. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized with bivariate random-effects models. Results Thirty-one studies including 2,344 patients undergoing imaging assessment were included. Seven external test cohorts, including 219 patient observations, entered the primary meta-analysis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.63-0.88), specificity was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.63-0.84), and summary area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.81 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.69-0.91). Internal test cohorts showed higher apparent performance than external cohorts (AUC, 0.91 vs 0.81), but the difference was not statistically significant (difference, -0.09; 95% CI, -0.22 to 0.02; P = 0.12). Risk of bias was frequently high or unclear, and reporting transparency was heterogeneous. Conclusions MRI-based machine learning showed moderate-to-good external validation performance for TP-versus-PsP discrimination, but evidence remains limited by small external test cohorts, bias, and incomplete reporting. Larger transparent multicenter validations are needed before routine clinical implementation.

title: Three-fraction preoperative stereotactic radiotherapy for resectable brain metastases: the phase 2 STEP trial.
abstract: Background Postoperative stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT) is the standard adjuvant treatment after resection of brain metastases. It nevertheless requires delineation of a dynamic postsurgical cavity, delays local treatment by 3 to 6 weeks (and thus resumption of systemic therapy) and carries substantial risks of radiation necrosis and leptomeningeal disease. Preoperative SRT targets an intact lesion and may address some of these limitations. Methods In this open-label, single-arm, multicenter phase 2 trial, eligible adults had a Karnofsky performance status ≥70 and up to four brain metastases, including one resectable lesion ≤5 cm, from breast, non-small cell lung, kidney, or digestive cancer or melanoma. Patients received preoperative SRT (three fractions of 7.7 Gy prescribed to the encompassing 70% isodose line, equivalent to 11Gy per fraction at the isocenter) followed by surgical resection within 3 days of the last fraction. The primary outcome was 6-month local control on centrally reviewed MRI. Secondary outcomes included index-lesion radiation necrosis, leptomeningeal disease, distant intracranial control, overall survival, toxicity, cognition, and quality of life. Results Of 73 patients assessed, 67 were eligible and 63 received both SRT and surgery. Median age was 62 years. At a median follow-up of 12.7 months, the 6-month local control rate was 100% (95% CI, 95%-100%), meeting the primary endpoint; the 12-month rate was 96.4% (95% CI, 87%-99%). No leptomeningeal disease occurred. The 1-year cumulative incidence of index-lesion radiation necrosis was 7% (95% CI, 2%-16%), meeting the key secondary endpoint. Distant intracranial failure occurred in 22 patients (35%); 12-month overall survival was 81.2% (95% CI, 70%-89%). Postoperative complications occurred in 4 patients (6.3%); cognition and quality of life remained stable over the 12 months of protocol follow-up. Conclusions Three-fraction preoperative SRT followed by resection was associated with high local control, low radiation necrosis, and no leptomeningeal disease, supporting evaluation in ongoing randomized trials.

In this open-label, single-arm, multicenter phase 2 trial, eligible adults had a Karnofsky performance status ≥70 and up to four brain metastases, including one resectable lesion ≤5 cm, from breast, non-small cell lung, kidney, or digestive cancer or melanoma. Patients received preoperative SRT (three fractions of 7.7 Gy prescribed to the encompassing 70% isodose line, equivalent to 11Gy per fraction at the isocenter) followed by surgical resection within 3 days of the last fraction. The primary outcome was 6-month local control on centrally reviewed MRI. Secondary outcomes included index-lesion radiation necrosis, leptomeningeal disease, distant intracranial control, overall survival, toxicity, cognition, and quality of life.

Results

Of 73 patients assessed, 67 were eligible and 63 received both SRT and surgery. Median age was 62 years. At a median follow-up of 12.7 months, the 6-month local control rate was 100% (95% CI, 95%-100%), meeting the primary endpoint; the 12-month rate was 96.4% (95% CI, 87%-99%). No leptomeningeal disease occurred. The 1-year cumulative incidence of index-lesion radiation necrosis was 7% (95% CI, 2%-16%), meeting the key secondary endpoint. Distant intracranial failure occurred in 22 patients (35%); 12-month overall survival was 81.2% (95% CI, 70%-89%). Postoperative complications occurred in 4 patients (6.3%); cognition and quality of life remained stable over the 12 months of protocol follow-up.

Conclusions

Three-fraction preoperative SRT followed by resection was associated with high local control, low radiation necrosis, and no leptomeningeal disease, supporting evaluation in ongoing randomized trials.

title: Longitudinal PET RANO 1.0 and RANO 2.0 response assessment in vorasidenib-treated IDH-mutant gliomas: the VORAFET study.
abstract: Background Conventional MRI may not fully reflect the biological activity of vorasidenib. PET may detect treatment-related metabolic changes before structural changes become evident on MRI. We evaluated longitudinal PET and MRI changes in patients with IDH-mutant gliomas receiving vorasidenib. Methods VORAFET is a longitudinal study of adults with IDH-mutant gliomas treated with vorasidenib. Eligible patients had predominantly non-enhancing WHO grade 2 or 3 gliomas, had not received prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was longitudinal metabolic and structural imaging response according to PET RANO 1.0 and RANO 2.0. Integrated [¹⁸F]FET PET/MRI was performed at baseline and every 3 months. Results Thirty-nine patients were included; at baseline, 23 and 29 had PET and MRI-measurable disease. As best response, PET RANO 1.0 identified 2 complete and 12 partial responses, yielding an ORR of 60.9%; median time to first response was 4.5 months (range 3-12 months). RANO 2.0 showed no complete or partial responses, whereas 5 patients achieved minor response at a median of 9 months (range 6-12 months). Progressive disease occurred in 6 of 39 patients (15.4%) according to PET RANO 1.0 and in 1 of 39 (2.6%) according to RANO 2.0. Patients with PET-PD more often had subtle contrast enhancement and showed higher baseline FLAIR volume, MTV, TBRmax, and TBRmean. Conclusions PET RANO 1.0 identified metabolic changes during vorasidenib treatment that were not always reflected by RANO 2.0 assessment. Longer follow-up is needed to clarify the relationship between PET metabolic changes and MRI findings and to determine their clinical significance.

title: Keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the distal Esophagus in a young adult woman with celiac disease: a case report.
abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) usually affects the upper or middle esophagus and is strongly associated with tobacco and alcohol use. We report a 28-year-old woman with longstanding celiac disease who presented with progressive dysphagia, weight loss, retrosternal pain, and melena. Endoscopy showed a partially obstructing distal esophageal mass; biopsy confirmed moderately differentiated keratinizing ESCC, while duodenal biopsy showed active celiac disease. CT and PET imaging revealed regional lymphadenopathy without distant metastasis. She underwent feeding jejunostomy, nutritional support, and neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, but follow-up imaging showed interval disease progression. The patient's young age, squamous cell histology in a distal esophagus, and the absence of conventional risk factors make this an unusual presentation. This case emphasizes the need for high clinical suspicion and early endoscopic evaluation in young patients with celiac disease presenting with alarming symptoms, even in the absence of classic risk factors for esophageal cancer.

title: Inflammatory Pseudotumor of the liver mimicking peritoneal Carcinomatosis: a diagnostic challenge.
abstract: Inflammatory pseudotumor of the liver is a rare benign entity with non-specific radiological features that can closely mimic malignant hepatic lesions, making its diagnosis challenging. We report the case of a patient in whom a focal hepatic lesion was detected on abdominal ultrasound, with imaging findings consistent with underlying cirrhosis. Subsequent contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated a dysmorphic liver with infiltrative subcapsular hepatic masses, associated with micronodular infiltration of the peritoneal fat and cardiophrenic angle lymphadenopathy, raising strong suspicion for a malignant hepatic process with peritoneal carcinomatosis. The diagnosis of inflammatory pseudotumor was ultimately confirmed by a CT-guided percutaneous liver biopsy. This case emphasizes the importance of considering inflammatory pseudotumor in the differential diagnosis of hepatic lesions, as this entity may closely mimic malignant etiologies on imaging.

title: An elusive cause of recurrent hypoglycemia: delayed diagnosis of insulinoma treated with curative distal pancreatectomy in a resource-limited setting.
abstract: A 43-year-old woman presented with recurrent hypoglycemia and episodes of loss of consciousness. On admission, her blood glucose was 37 mg/dL (reference range: 70-99 mg/dl), with recovery after intravenous dextrose, fulfilling Whipple's triad. She had a two-year history of dizziness, fatigue, diaphoresis, and neuroglycopenic symptoms, often relieved by frequent soft drink intake, leading to weight gain. She was previously misdiagnosed with a neurologic disorder, resulting in delayed evaluation. Laboratory findings showed elevated serum insulin levels of 65 μU/mL (reference range: 2.6-24.9 μU/mL) during hypoglycemia. Contrast-enhanced CT identified a 1.7 × 1.3 cm mass in the pancreatic body without metastasis. The patient underwent distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy. Postoperatively, hypoglycemic episodes resolved completely. Histopathology confirmed insulinoma. This case highlights the importance of considering insulinoma in patients with recurrent hypoglycemia. Delayed diagnosis may occur due to nonspecific symptoms and misdiagnosis. Careful clinical assessment, basic biochemical testing, and imaging can facilitate timely diagnosis and effective surgical management in resource-limited settings.

title: Left pulmonary aplasia with ipsilateral renal agenesis and double superior vena cava in a term neonate: a case report.
abstract: Background Unilateral pulmonary agenesis/aplasia is rare and often accompanied by extrapulmonary anomalies that affect prognosis. Case report A term male neonate delivered by cesarean section for fetal distress required brief invasive ventilation and was subsequently stabilized. Chest radiography revealed left hemithorax opacification. Contrast-enhanced CT on day 4 demonstrated a reduced left hemithorax with an absent left pulmonary parenchyma, a blind-ending left main bronchus, and an absent ipsilateral pulmonary arterial supply, consistent with left pulmonary aplasia. Evaluation also identified left renal agenesis with compensatory right renal hypertrophy and double superior vena cava, with discordant drainage descriptions across modalities requiring confirmation. The infant transitioned to room air, established feeds, and was discharged clinically stable on day 9 after birth. Conclusion Definitive anatomic characterization of unilateral thoracic opacity in neonates should prompt systematic cardiovascular and genitourinary screening and coordinated multidisciplinary follow-up in an outpatient setting.

title: Durable response to vebreltinib in heavily pretreated MET-amplified intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: a case report.
abstract: Background MET amplification, although detected in only 2%-5% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinomas (ICC), represents an actionable oncogenic driver. Treatment options after failure of first-line immunochemotherapy remain limited, and clinical data on vebreltinib, a novel highly selective MET inhibitor, in this molecular subset are scarce. Case presentation A 61-year-old woman with metastatic ICC harboring high-level MET amplification (tissue gene copy number, 26.79) experienced disease progression on first-line durvalumab plus gemcitabine/cisplatin, second-line liposomal irinotecan/fluorouracil plus lenvatinib and durvalumab, radiotherapy, and transarterial chemoembolization. Following a brief period of vebreltinib (200 mg twice daily) plus durvalumab that was interrupted by grade 4 myelosuppression, the patient continued on vebreltinib monotherapy after hematologic recovery. Restaging computed tomography demonstrated a partial response (PR), with carbohydrate antigen 19-9 normalizing (a 99.2% reduction). This response lasted over 6 months until eventual disease progression. Conclusion To our knowledge, this is the first report of vebreltinib monotherapy inducing a deep and durable partial response in heavily pretreated, MET-amplified ICC, with the response lasting over 6 months despite eventual disease progression. This case underscores the critical value of comprehensive molecular profiling after first-line treatment failure to identify actionable drivers such as MET amplification.

title: Hormone Receptor-Positive HER2-Negative Oligometastatic Breast Cancer: prognostic stratification and pattern of progression.
abstract: Background The management of oligometastatic breast cancer (OMBC) remains controversial, particularly regarding selection for local ablative treatment (LAT). In HR+/HER2- OMBC, where prolonged survival is often the case, improved stratification and characterization of progression may guide treatment. We aimed to define prognostic subsets, assess the contribution of Modern-Imaging-Methods (MIMs; 18F-FDG-PET/CT or WB-MRI) to LAT selection, and describe progression after first-line therapy in these subgroups of patients. Materials and methods All consecutive patients with HR+/HER2- OMBC treated at our institution between 2012 and 2020 were included. OMBC was defined as ≤ 5 metastases. Prognostic factors including biological subtype, anatomical distribution, imaging modality, and LAT were evaluated for overall and progression-free survival (OS, PFS). Results Among 145 patients (median follow-up 82.8 months), median OS and PFS were, respectively, 81.1 and 26.5 months. Luminal-A-like subtypes, absence of liver metastases, and use of MIMs independently predicted better survival. LAT improved PFS (hazard ratio [HR]=0.52; 95%CI[0.29-0.91], p=0.0233) and showed a trend toward longer OS. In patients staged with MIMs, LAT significantly improved both OS (HR = 0.29; 95%CI[0.12-0.73], p=0.008) and PFS (HR = 0.40; 95%CI[0.21-0.77], p=0.0064). After first-line systemic therapy, only 18% developed polymetastatic progression. Conclusion In HR+/HER2- OMBC, three actionable considerations emerge: staging must incorporate modern imaging to accurately define metastatic burden; LAT may be considered in selected patients with low-grade disease, absence of liver metastases, and long disease-free interval; in oligoprogression after first-line therapy, LAT should be re-evaluated within a multidisciplinary setting. These data offer pragmatic benchmarks to individualize treatment while awaiting definitive randomized evidence.

title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Tumor-Derived DNA Analysis Aids in the Diagnosis of Postpartum Diffuse Midline Glioma.
abstract: Background Gliomas diagnosed during pregnancy or postpartum pose diagnostic and management challenges. Neurologic symptoms may be attributed to physiological changes of pregnancy or the postpartum state, possibly delaying evaluation. When lesions arise in high-risk locations, such as the brainstem, tissue biopsy is frequently infeasible, further complicating the diagnostic process. Patient presentation A 28-year-old woman developed dysphagia during pregnancy, which persisted and gradually worsened after delivery. Postpartum evaluation identified a right thyroid nodule, subsequently diagnosed as papillary thyroid carcinoma following hemithyroidectomy. Eight months postpartum, the patient experienced progressive dysphagia, headaches, and dizziness. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed an expansile medullary lesion concerning for a high-grade primary brainstem tumor. Due to the brainstem location, biopsy was infeasible, and empiric chemoradiation was initiated for presumed high-grade glioma. Molecular findings Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tumor-derived nucleic acid analysis using Summit™ 2.0 identified an H3-3A K28M alteration, along with co-occurring pathogenic alterations in NF1 and TP53. In conjunction with the clinical and radiographic findings, these molecular results supported classification of the tumor as diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered. Management and outcome Following completion of chemoradiation, dordaviprone therapy was initiated. At the most recent documented follow-up in January 2026, brain MRI demonstrated decreased size and enhancement of the medullary lesion, accompanied by improvement in dysphagia, headaches, dystonic movements, balance, and overall performance status. Conclusions This case demonstrates that cerebrospinal fluid-based genomic profiling can provide clinically meaningful molecular information when tissue diagnosis is contraindicated and can inform treatment planning for patients with anatomically inaccessible central nervous system tumors. Gliomas diagnosed during pregnancy or postpartum pose diagnostic and management challenges. Neurologic symptoms may be attributed to physiological changes of pregnancy or the postpartum state, possibly delaying evaluation. A 28-year-old woman developed dysphagia during pregnancy, which persisted and gradually worsened after delivery. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tumor-derived nucleic acid analysis using Summit™ 2.0 identified an H3-3A K28M alteration, along with co-occurring pathogenic alterations in NF1 and TP53. Following completion of chemoradiation, dordaviprone therapy was initiated. title: Pelvic Insufficiency Fractures After Chemoradiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Incidence, Long-Term Outcomes, and Survivorship Management.
abstract: Pelvic insufficiency fractures, a late complication of chemoradiotherapy for cervical cancer, can cause pain and functional impairment. Although most studies have reported incidence rates and risk factors, few have examined clinical presentation, long-term symptom burden, or the impact on survivorship. We conducted a retrospective study of patients with cervical cancer treated with chemoradiotherapy from 2018 to 2024. We extracted clinical characteristics, treatment details, dosimetric parameters, imaging studies documenting pelvic insufficiency fractures, and clinical outcomes from the electronic medical record. We used the Kaplan-Meier method to estimate the probability of pelvic insufficiency fractures and univariate Cox regression to assess clinical and dosimetric factors associated with their development. The cohort comprised 153 patients (median follow-up: 41.4 months). After chemoradiotherapy, 18 patients (11.8%) developed radiologically confirmed pelvic insufficiency fractures (median time to diagnosis: 9.5 months; probability of pelvic insufficiency fracture at 24 months: 11.4%). PET-CT and/or MRI showed that most pelvic insufficiency fractures involved the sacrum. No statistically significant clinical or dosimetric predictors of pelvic insufficiency fractures were identified. All symptomatic patients (n = 15, 83%) required referral to pain-management services (median observed duration of symptoms: 37 months). No symptomatic patient achieved documented complete symptom resolution during the available follow-up. Most pelvic insufficiency fractures presented with new-onset pelvic or sacral pain within two years of completing chemoradiotherapy. The lack of clinical or dosimetric predictors suggests a multifactorial etiology of fracture risk. Persistent pain, despite multimodal supportive care, led to long-term morbidity. These findings underscore the need for prospective studies to develop evidence-based preventive strategies, survivorship assessments, and management pathways.

title: Quadruple-negative autoantibody status and interstitial lung disease progression in systemic sclerosis.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the association between disease-specific autoantibody profiles and disease progression in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD), with a focus on a quadruple-negative phenotype. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 80 patients with SSc-ILD who were followed for at least 12 months at a single tertiary centre. ILD progression was defined according to the OMERACT criteria and/or worsening on high-resolution computed tomography. Autoantibody status was categorized based on four antibodies: anti-topoisomerase I, anti-centromere, anti-RNA polymerase III and anti-U1-RNP. Quadruple-negative (QN) was defined as negativity for all four antibodies. Factors associated with ILD progression were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Exploratory comprehensive autoantibody profiling was performed in patients with available stored serum samples. Results During a median follow-up of 44.5 months, disease progression occurred in 32 of 80 patients with SSc-ILD. Anti-centromere antibody (ACA) positivity was associated with a lower risk of progression, whereas anti-topoisomerase I antibody positivity was not associated with disease progression (Model 2: OR 3.19, 95% CI 0.70-14.60). Compared with ACA positivity, QN status was associated with ILD progression (Model 2: OR 10.40, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.77-60.70). However, CIs were wide. Exploratory analyses showed a high prevalence of anti-Ro-52 antibody positivity among patients with QN status. Conclusion QN autoantibody status may be associated with an increased risk of ILD progression in SSc. The QN status may represent a heterogeneous serological category that could help identify patients who require closer clinical monitoring. However, these results are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, independent cohorts.

title: Cardiovascular risk stratification using chest CT in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of incidentally detected coronary artery calcification (CAC) on routine chest computed tomography (CT) for cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM). Methods In this single-centre cross-sectional study, adult patients with IIM who underwent noncardiac, nongated high-resolution chest CT (HRCT) were included. CAC was visually categorized as absent, mild, moderate, or severe. Diagnostic performance for established coronary artery disease (CAD) and established cardiovascular (CV) events was assessed. Kaplan-Meier analyses evaluated CV death-free survival, and multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with CAC. A matched systemic sclerosis (SSc) cohort served as validation cohort. Results Among 234 patients with IIM (mean age 57.1±15.9 years; 70.1% female), CAC was present in 43.2%. Higher CAC thresholds showed greater specificity for established CAD and prior CV events, whereas lower thresholds were more sensitive. CAC was associated with reduced CV death-free survival (log-rank p = 0.0095), with a stepwise decline across CAC severity categories. Findings were similar in the matched SSc cohort. Increasing CAC burden was associated with older age, smoking, higher CV risk burden, interstitial lung disease, and higher disease activity. In adjusted analyses, high disease activity was independently associated with moderate CAC (OR 4.01, 95% CI 1.29-12.50), while a higher number of concomitant DMARDs was associated with severe CAC (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.27-5.11). Conclusion Incidentally detected CAC on routine chest CT provides diagnostic and prognostic information in IIM and may represent a pragmatic approach to improve cardiovascular risk stratification in this high-risk population.

title: Design and shielding effectiveness of adjustable modular medical radiation shelter.
abstract: Medical imaging and radiotherapy rely on ionizing radiation that must be contained to protect staff, patients, and the public. Conventional shielding rooms use permanent, immobile concrete walls that are slow to build, leaving primary clinics and emergency sites poorly served. A modular, adjustable shelter was designed with six-sided composite walls combining barite-paraffin, a 24-cm water layer, and 0.5-20-mm lead plates for synergistic photon and neutron shielding, with S/Z-shaped penetrations to suppress joint leakage. Per the Chinese diagnostic radiology standard GBZ 130-2020, analytical models predicted shielding of 70-150 kVp diagnostic X-rays and 6 MV photons and an 11.9-fold reduction of 2 MeV neutrons. Geant4 Monte Carlo validation across six clinical scenarios (39 keV-1.47 MeV photons, 2 MeV neutrons) reproduced the model within 2.5% at 511 keV; exterior ambient dose equivalent H*(10) remained below 0.5 μSv h-1, satisfying the GBZ 130-2020 public dose limit. The shelter provides flexible, rapidly deployable protection for routine and emergency medical use.

title: Neuroanatomical Subtypes of Schizophrenia Reveal Divergent Atrophy Trajectories and Distinct Associations with Long-Term Clozapine Use.
abstract: Background and hypothesis Schizophrenia is a heterogeneous disorder, and biology-informed stratification may provide insights into individual differences in disease course and treatment response. We hypothesized that neuroimaging-based subtyping could reveal biologically distinct subgroups characterized by divergent brain atrophy trajectories and unique clinical profiles. Study design We applied the Subtype and Stage Inference framework to baseline structural MRI data from the 6-year longitudinal Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis cohort (n = 467), including patients, unaffected siblings and healthy controls. We characterized subtype-specific longitudinal brain atrophy and medication profiles. Subtype-specific atrophy patterns were correlated with external molecular maps of neurotransmitter density and schizophrenia-related gene expression. Study results Two distinct neuroanatomical subtypes were identified: subtype 1 (65.5%), characterized by widespread cortical volume loss at baseline, and stable volume decrease over 6-year follow-up. Conversely, subtype 2 (34.5%) showed baseline volume decrease confined in the hippocampus and amygdala, but accelerated volume loss over follow-up. Clinically, subtype 1 patients had a significantly higher prevalence of clozapine use than subtype 2 (36% vs. 17%; chi2 = 5.62, P = 0.02), and brain atrophy of subtype 1 mirrored patterns observed in clozapine users. The two subtypes showed divergent spatial associations with neurotransmitter systems and risk-gene expression profiles. Conclusions We identified two neuroanatomical subtypes of schizophrenia showing divergent brain atrophy over 6-years. The subtypes may represent biologically distinct forms of schizophrenia, as they show different medication profiles and associations with molecular signatures. Our results provide a candidate framework for parsing disease heterogeneity and may offer insights for future stratified treatment strategies.

title: Neuroimaging of Clinical High-Risk Youth From the Kenya Psychosis-Risk Outcomes Study (KePROS): Regional Structural Analyses and Vertexwise Cortical Deviation Mapping (VCDM).
abstract: Background and hypothesis There are no neuroimaging studies of individuals at clinical high risk (CHR) for psychosis in Africa. Using the Kenya Psychosis-Risk Outcomes Study (KePROS), we examined cortical and subcortical morphometry in CHR individuals using conventional regional measures and Vertexwise Cortical Deviation Mapping (VCDM), a surface-based method quantifying extreme cortical thickness deviations. Study design Seventy-four CHR participants and 42 healthy controls (HCs), aged 18-26, underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging on a 3 T scanner in Nairobi. Regional cortical thickness and subcortical volumes were derived using FreeSurfer. Vertexwise Cortical Deviation Mapping quantified the proportion of cortical vertices exhibiting abnormally thin or thick cortex across standardized deviation thresholds (1-3 SD). title: The Efficacy of Erector Spinae Plane Block Versus Subcostal Transversus Abdominis Plane Block in Laparoscopic Nephrectomy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Objectives This study compared the efficacy and safety of erector spinae plane block (ESPB) versus subcostal transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block in reducing postoperative pain among patients undergoing laparoscopic nephrectomy. Methods This randomized clinical trial enrolled 70 adult patients, ASA physical status I or II, who underwent total (radical) laparoscopic nephrectomy under general anesthesia. Patients were randomly assigned to 2 groups. Group ESPB received an ultrasound-guided ESPB at the T7 transverse process level, while group TAP received an ultrasound-guided subcostal TAP block. The primary outcome was the total amount of morphine consumed at 6 and 24 hours postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of patients requiring opioid analgesia, time to rescue analgesia, visual analog scale of pain intensity, time to postoperative ambulation, intraoperative and postoperative hemodynamics, arterial partial pressure of oxygen to fraction of inspired oxygen (PaO 2 /FiO 2 or P /F) ratio, and incidence of complications. Results Compared with the TAP group, the ESPB group exhibited significantly lower median morphine consumption at 24 hours ( P =0.032), prolonged time to first analgesic rescue ( P =0.049), and lower incidence of rescue morphine requirement (OR=0.23; 95% CI=0.06-0.94; P =0.031), with lower visual analog scale pain scores at 12, 18, and 24 hours postoperatively ( P <0.001). The mean arterial blood pressure and heart rates were comparable between groups. No significant adverse effects from either approach. Discussion In laparoscopic nephrectomy, ultrasound-guided ESPB may safely and effectively be used to improve pain management and reduce pain intensity, with stable hemodynamics and a comparable risk of postoperative complications to the ultrasound-guided subcostal TAP block.

title: Neonatal Cardiac Tamponade Related to Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter: A Rare Case Report.
abstract: Background Peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are commonly used in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) to provide prolonged intravenous access for preterm and critically ill infants. They are generally preferred over surgically placed central venous catheters because of easier insertion and, in some settings, lower infection rates. However, rare but life-threatening complications may occur. Cardiac tamponade, resulting from catheter malposition or delayed migration with perforation of the superior vena cava (SVC) or cardiac wall, is one such complication. This case highlights the need for vigilant monitoring even when initial catheter placement is confirmed as correct. Clinical findings A male infant born at 32 weeks' gestation with intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) required mechanical ventilation and surfactant therapy. A PICC was inserted through the right radial vein, and radiographic assessment confirmed appropriate positioning in the SVC. The infant initially improved. On day 10 of NICU admission, he developed sudden respiratory distress, hypotonia, bradycardia, and cardiovascular collapse. Diagnosis Echocardiography demonstrated severe pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade due to SVC perforation by the PICC tip. Intervention and outcome The catheter was immediately removed, and emergency pericardiocentesis was performed. Despite aggressive resuscitation, the infant died on day 11 of life. Practice recommendations Delayed perforation can occur days after apparently correct placement. Preventive strategies should include risk-stratified catheter positioning, preference for lower SVC tip placement, routine echocardiographic surveillance especially after the first week and enhanced staff training for early recognition of warning signs. Continuous quality improvement and readiness for emergency intervention are essential to improve neonatal outcomes.

title: Feasibility of opportunistic osteoporosis screening using ankle CT Hounsfield units in older adults with ankle fractures.
abstract: Background Fragility fractures reveal osteoporosis, but ankle fractures are not consistently defined as fragility fractures. CT-derived Hounsfield unit measurements may provide an opportunistic method to identify patients at risk for osteoporosis. Purpose This study investigated the relationship between Hounsfield units (HU) from ankle CT scans and bone mineral density (BMD) measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA), with the aim of determining whether sufficient signal exists between ankle HU and DEXA-derived BMD to justify a larger prospective validation study, rather than to establish a definitive diagnostic tool. Study design/level of evidence Retrospective correlation study. Level III. Methods Patients aged 55 years or older, who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for OTA/AO 44 A-C ankle fractures between 2012 and 2024 and had both a preoperative ankle CT and a DEXA scan within 1 year of injury, were reviewed. HU values of the distal tibia and fibula were measured using standardized elliptical regions of interest. Multivariate linear regression was performed with the lowest DEXA T-score as the dependent variable, with HU values, and BMI as independent variables. Results A total of 57 patients (87.7% female, mean age 69.67 ± 9.24 years) were included. The average ankle HU was 192.43 ± 60.04, and the mean T-score was -1.73 ± 0.96. Regression analysis demonstrated that HU values (B = 0.005, P = .021) and BMI (B = 0.064, P = .007) were positively correlated with the T-score.The regression model was lowest T-score = 0.005*Ankle HU + 0.064*BMI-4.422.Based on this equation, an HU measurement of 106.64 or less, assuming a BMI of 21.7, correlated with osteoporosis. Conclusions Ankle HU values from CT scans demonstrated a positive association with DEXA-derived BMD, supporting proof-of-concept for ankle HU as a preliminary screening tool and providing methodological groundwork for future prospective validation. Given the high prevalence of osteopenia or osteoporosis in this population, ankle fractures should prompt formal bone health evaluation.

title: A pilot study of a computed tomography volumetric analysis technique to determine severity of injury and prognosis for OTA 42A-C open tibial diaphyseal fractures.
abstract: Purpose This pilot study evaluated a novel computed tomography (CT)-based volumetric analysis tool for open tibial fractures. We hypothesized that the volumetric injury ratio (VINJ/VUNINJ), a quantitative comparison of injured with contralateral uninjured limb segments, would correlate with clinical outcomes and serve as a prognostic marker. Methods A retrospective review of a tibial fracture registry was conducted at a single academic institution (2014-2024). Eligible patients were older than 18 years old with preoperative bilateral lower extremity CT imaging, high-energy injuries, and ≥6 months of follow-up. Demographics, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), injury features, and outcomes including fracture-related infection (FRI), amputation, and nonunion were collected. Tissue volume was measured at the fracture midpoint and 5 cm proximal and distal, with corresponding contralateral measurements. VINJ/VUNINJ was calculated, and logistic regression estimated complication risk. The primary endpoint was a composite complication (FRI, amputation, or nonunion). Discrimination was assessed using AUROC and compared with the Gustilo-Anderson (GA) classification via the DeLong test. The Youden Index identified an optimal risk threshold. Power analysis estimated sample size requirements for a future validation study. Results Fifteen patients met inclusion criteria (mean age 36.1 ± 13.5 years). GA distribution: 60% II, 6.7% IIIa, 26.7% IIIb, and 6.7% IIIc. The volumetric model (log[p/(1-p)] = -110.964 + 100.011 × VINJ/VUNINJ) demonstrated a trend toward improved discriminatory ability compared with the GA model (AUROC: 0.944 vs 0.769, P = 0.068). A Youden-derived threshold (0.539) classified 5 patients (33.3%) as high-risk; all developed complications compared with 10% in the low-risk group (100% vs 10%, P = 0.001). Power analysis indicated that detecting a twofold increase in complications would require ∼23 patients per arm (46 total). Conclusion This pilot study introduces a CT-based volumetric ratio as a quantitative tool for risk stratification in open tibial fractures. Findings suggest superior prognostic accuracy compared with GA, supporting prospective validation in larger patient cohorts.

title: What is the Rate of Occult Vessel Abnormalities in High-Energy Tibial Plateau Fractures (OTA/AO 41)?
abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to determine the rate of occult vascular abnormalities in high-energy tibial plateau fractures using computed tomography angiography (CTA). Methods . Design Prospective Cohort Study. Setting Single Academic Level I Trauma Center. Patient selection criteria Adult patients with a tibial plateau (OTA/AO 41) fracture, without clinical indication for CTA, that underwent knee-spanning external fixation were prospectively enrolled. Outcome measures and comparisons After external fixation, patients underwent CTA to evaluate fracture morphology and the vascular tree. Fisher exact test was used to determine correlations between arterial abnormalities and wound complications in patients with ≥90 days of follow-up. Results A total of 26 patients with 27 high-energy tibial plateau fractures were enrolled. Patients were predominantly male (n = 16, 61.5%) with a mean age of 45.1 ± 13.3 years. All patients had a blunt injury mechanism resulting in mostly closed (n = 25, 92.6%), bicondylar (n = 22, 81.5%) tibial plateau fractures. CTA demonstrated nonatherosclerosis vascular abnormalities in 3 patients (11.5%). Two had disrupted flow in the popliteal artery, and 1 had disrupted flow in the anterior tibial artery. No patient required vascular intervention. Atherosclerosis was appreciated in 6 (26.9%) patients. One of 3 patients (33%) with nonatherosclerosis vascular abnormalities had wound complications. Four of 24 patients (16.7%) without nonatherosclerosis vascular abnormalities had wound complications. There was no significant correlation between nonatherosclerosis vascular abnormalities and wound complications (abnormality present: 33.3% wound complication rate vs. no abnormality: 16.7%, P = 0.47). Conclusions Non atherosclerotic vascular abnormalities on CTA were found in approximately a 10th of high-energy tibial plateau fractures. In this cohort, vascular abnormalities were not associated with wound complications. CTA is likely not necessary in patients with tibial plateau fracture without clinical indications for CTA. Level of evidence Prognostic Level IV. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Outcomes Following Early Weight Bearing in Syndesmotic Injuries: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Objectives To compare outcomes of early weight bearing (EWB) at 2-weeks versus delayed weight bearing (DWB) at 6-weeks following operative ankle fracture fixation with syndesmotic stabilization. Methods Design: Prospective randomized controlled clinical trial. Setting Single Level 1 Trauma Center. Patient selection criteria Adult patients with operative rotational ankle fractures (OTA/AO 44A-C) and an intraoperative finding of syndesmotic injury following fracture fixation between September 2019 and September 2022 were included. All underwent dynamic syndesmotic stabilization utilizing a single suture button. Exclusion criteria were fibular fractures not amenable to length-stable fixation (e.g., Maisonneuve injuries), neuropathic diabetes, body weight ≥147.4 kg (325 lbs), imprisonment, pregnancy, lactation, end-stage renal disease, cognitive dysfunction, or polytrauma. Outcome measures and comparisons Maintenance of syndesmotic reduction at 1 year comparing immediate postoperative and 1-year CT scans of both ankles was the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes: pain (VAS), surgical satisfaction (SSQ-8), functional scores (AAOS Foot and Ankle), ankle range of motion, and complications. Results 106 patients were enrolled: 40 underwent syndesmotic fixation and were randomized. 16 patients (mean age 41 (21-80), 9 female, 7 male) randomized to EWB and 23 (mean age 43 (23-85), 12 female, 11 male) to DWB completed the study. Fracture types included lateral malleolar (OTA/AO 44A), bimalleolar and bimalleolar equivalent (OTA/AO 44B), and trimalleolar (OTA/AO 44C) fractures, with similar distribution between groups (p=0.96). EWB group had significantly higher pain scores (4.6 ± 2.8 vs 2.8 ± 2.3, p = 0.039) at the 2-week visit compared to DWB. At 1 year, dorsiflexion in the EWB group was significantly higher (14.2° ± 3.9° vs 7.7° ± 4.4°) than the DWB (p = 0.017). No significant difference in syndesmotic malreduction (p>0.99), loss of reduction (p>0.89), PROs, development of arthritis (p>1.0) or complication rates (p>0.37) at any other timepoint. Conclusions Early weight bearing at 2-weeks was noninferior to delayed weight bearing at 6-weeks following rotational ankle fracture fixation with a syndesmotic injury stabilized with flexible fixation. Level of evidence Level I.

title: Is the use of Porous Threaded Titanium Implants Associated with Lower Rates of Implant Migration in Elderly Pelvic Ring Injuries?
abstract: Objectives To determine if porous threaded titanium implant (PTTI) screws placed in the posterior pelvic ring as iliosacral (IS) or transiliac-transsacral (transsacral) were associated with implant positional changes, alterations in postoperative weightbearing restrictions, or the necessity of revision surgery in operatively managed geriatric pelvic ring injuries, compared to standard stainless steel screws. Methods Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Academic Level I trauma center. Patient selection criteria Patients with operatively managed pelvic ring injuries (AO/OTA61) from January 2017 to June 2025, aged ≥65 years with a minimum of 6-months of radiographic and clinical follow-up were included.Outcome Measures and Comparisons: The primary study outcome was the incidence of postoperative pelvic ring implant positional changes, ≥2mm from immediate postoperative radiographs compared among patients treated with PTTI versus standard stainless steel screws for IS and transsacral fixation. Secondary outcomes included subsequent revision surgery or alterations in postoperative weightbearing restrictions related to implant positional changes. A multivariable logistic regression was used to determine associations of demographic, injury, and treatment variables with implant positional changes, the necessity for revision surgery, or negative changes in postoperative weightbearing restrictions. Results 271 patients were included; 215 (79.3%) were managed with standard screws, while PTTIs were used in 56 (20.7%). The standard screw cohort had a median follow-up of 8.9 months (interquartile range 6.2-11.3 months), while the PTTI cohort had a median follow-up of 9.1 months (interquartile range 6.3-10.9 months). title: Preoperative ultrasound in pediatric supracondylar fracture-related nerve injuries: intraoperative correlation in a tertiary referral retrospective case series.
abstract: Nerve palsy is a recognized complication of paediatric supracondylar humeral fractures. Most injuries recover spontaneously, a subset require surgical exploration, and identifying those who may benefit from intervention remains challenging. High-resolution ultrasound has emerged as a potential adjunct for assessing nerve injury, although its utility in this setting remains incompletely defined. A retrospective case series was conducted at a tertiary peripheral nerve injury center. Children less than 16 years with persistent supracondylar fracture-related nerve palsy who underwent preoperative ultrasound and surgical exploration between 2018 and 2024 were included. Ultrasound findings were categorized as structural abnormality, compression/tethering, neuroma/swelling, or entrapment and were compared with intraoperative findings. Analysis was descriptive, focusing on ultrasound detection of nerve abnormality and concordance with surgical findings. Twenty-two patients were included (mean age: 7 years). All had surgically confirmed nerve pathology. Ultrasound demonstrated nerve abnormality in 21 out of 22 cases (95%). Compression/tethering was the most common finding (18/22), followed by structural abnormality (14/22), neuroma/swelling (7/22), and entrapment (2/22). Intraoperatively, structural abnormalities were identified in 17 cases, compression/tethering in 21, neuroma in 3, and entrapment in 4. Ultrasound frequently identified nerve abnormality but demonstrated variable concordance with intraoperative findings, including overestimation of neuroma (7 vs. 3 cases) and under-detection of entrapment (2 vs. 4 cases). Preoperative ultrasound frequently demonstrated abnormal nerve features in children with persistent palsy following supracondylar humeral fracture. However, its limited concordance in characterizing specific pathology restricts its role as a standalone decision-making tool. Ultrasound findings should be interpreted alongside clinical assessment when considering surgical exploration.

title: Subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium in adolescent athletes with acute groin pain: clinical and MRI features of a radiograph-occult injury pattern.
abstract: Subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium is an uncommon MRI finding in young athletes with acute groin pain and is frequently occult on plain radiographs. This study aimed to characterize its clinical presentation, MRI findings, associated injuries, and return-to-sport outcomes. This retrospective single-center case series included athletes aged ≤22 years who underwent MRI for acute sports-related groin pain with negative or inconclusive radiographs between 2017 and 2025. Patients meeting predefined MRI criteria for subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium were identified, and clinical, imaging, and outcome data were analyzed descriptively. Twenty of 91 patients (22.0%) met the MRI criteria. Their mean age was 13.9 ± 1.5 years, 19 (95%) were male, and 18 (90%) had open physes. Periosteal elevation was present in all patients, and 19 (95%) demonstrated a predominantly subperiosteal fluid collection, most commonly with a lentiform configuration. Associated anterior inferior iliac spine avulsion injury or intramuscular iliacus injury was identified in 10 patients (50%). All patients were managed nonoperatively and returned to unrestricted sports participation after progressive rehabilitation at a mean of 4.5 ± 2.2 weeks. Subperiosteal hematoma of the ilium is a reproducible MRI finding in predominantly skeletally immature athletes with acute sports-related groin pain and negative or inconclusive radiographs. Recognition of periosteal elevation with a predominantly subperiosteal fluid collection may facilitate diagnosis of this radiograph-occult injury pattern. Although the underlying injury mechanism remains hypothetical, prospective studies are needed to clarify its clinical significance.

title: Open Reduction for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip in the Newborn Hip Screening Era: Changing Patient Characteristics and Surgical Strategies Without Compromising Outcomes.
abstract: Introduction Newborn hip ultrasound scan (USS) for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) has significantly reduced the number of delayed cases. However, open reduction (OR) is still required when nonsurgical treatment fails in properly screened patients, as well as in neglected and late-presenting cases. The aim of this study is to compare the clinical and radiologic outcomes of OR for DDH between screened and neglected cases. Methods Patients diagnosed with DDH and who underwent OR at a single center were included and categorized into 2 groups: Screened patients with an unsuccessful nonoperative treatment attempt (group 1), and neglected patients due to misdiagnosis or lack of USS (group 2). Comparisons were performed between groups for demographic parameters, surgical characteristics, pre- and postoperative radiographic analyses, radiologic and clinical outcome assessments, and complications. Results One hundred thirteen patients (148 hips) were included (group 1=66 and group 2=82). Group 1 had younger median age at the time of OR (11 vs. 23.2 mo, P<0.001), less IHDI grade 3-4 ratio (74% vs. 90%, P<0.001) higher medial/anterior OR ratio (55% vs. 15%, P<0.001), lower rate of concomitant femoral (35% vs. 71%, P<0.001) and pelvic osteotomy (38% vs. 78%, P<0.001) as compared with group 2. PFGD (proximal femur growth disturbance) rates were similar between the 2 groups. No difference noted for Severin grade (good to excellent result 89% vs. 92%, P=0.42), McKay (excellent result 83% vs. 77%, P=0.21), revision (9.8% vs. 6.4%, P=0.33), reoperation for implant removal (14 vs. 20, P=0.23), and for pelvic osteotomy due to residual acetabular dysplasia (6 vs. 5, P=0.58). Conclusion Early detection of DDH through USS not only reduced delayed presentations but also altered the demographic, clinical, and surgical characteristics of patients requiring OR. Despite failed initial conservative management, screened patients achieved comparable radiologic and clinical outcomes to those of unscreened patients, with similar rates of complications and residual acetabular dysplasia. These findings suggest that newborn hip USS enables less extensive surgical management without compromising outcomes. Level of evidence Level III-retrospective comparative study.

title: Development of Screening Criteria to Detect Transthyretin Amyloid in the Ligamentum Flavum: Early Detection of Amyloidosis.
abstract: Study design Prospective cross-sectional study. Objective To develop and apply screening criteria for patients at risk of systemic amyloidosis undergoing routine lumbar decompression, using histopathological evaluation of ligamentum flavum (LF) tissue. Summary of background data Amyloidosis is the extracellular deposition of insoluble, misfolded proteins, leading to progressive multiorgan dysfunction. Although recent therapies can slow disease progression, they do not reverse existing organ damage, underscoring the importance of early detection. Musculoskeletal manifestations of amyloidosis, such as lumbar stenosis (LS), can precede cardiac symptoms, providing an opportunity for early detection and treatment. Amyloid deposition within the LF has been identified as a contributing factor to LF hypertrophy and spinal stenosis, yet no standardized guidelines exist for determining which patients should undergo LF tissue sampling during lumbar decompression surgery. Methods Patients with conditions linked to amyloidosis and axial T2 magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) LF thickness >4.9 mm were prospectively enrolled. LF tissue samples were stained with Congo red (CR), and positive cases were subtyped. Patients with confirmed amyloid were referred for cardiac evaluation. Results Fifty patients were enrolled in the study; 14 (28%) had positive CR staining, and 10 (20%) were determined to have transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR) (95% CI, 17.5-41.7% and 11.2-33.0%, respectively). LF was thicker in the positive cohort (6.3±0.6 vs. 5.6±0.8; P≤.001). There was no difference in age or number of levels decompressed. Six of the 14 patients elected to undergo further cardiac evaluation, including a 99mTc-PYP scan; all results were negative. Conclusion The screening criteria identified patients at risk for amyloidosis. 20% of patients were found to have ATTR, and those who completed cardiac evaluation had no evidence of cardiac involvement at the time of evaluation. While larger studies are needed, LF analysis during routine decompression may provide a practical method for early detection.

title: Development of a Multivariable Prognostic Model for Risk Stratification in C1 Fractures.
abstract: Study design Retrospective analysis of adult patients with radiographically confirmed C1 fractures treated across a single healthcare system including multiple level 1 trauma centers and multiple community hospitals (2015-22). The primary outcome was instability. Peri-operative outcomes and complications were also considered. Objective To evaluate radiographic and clinical predictors of instability or surgical management in patients with C1 fractures and to develop a multivariable prognostic model. Summary of background data Determining instability in C1 fractures remains challenging. Traditional criteria rely heavily on radiographic displacement thresholds, which may not fully capture the multifactorial nature of atlas fracture instability. Methods Demographic, clinical, and radiographic variables were analyzed including lateral mass displacement, dens fracture, neurologic deficit, age, sex, and body mass index. Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression was used to adjust for confounders and identify factors significantly associated with instability/operative treatment. Receiver operating characteristic analysis assessed model discrimination. A point-based instability risk score was derived from model coefficients. Results In adjusted analysis of Two hundred and seventy-nine patients, Lateral mass displacement (OR 1.20 per mm, 95% CI 1.09-1.33, P<0.001), dens fracture (OR 2.67, 95% CI 1.35-5.38, P=0.0047), and neurologic deficit (OR 5.22, 95% CI 1.69-16.1, P=0.0047) were significantly associated with instability or surgical management. The traditional 7-mm displacement threshold performed poorly (AUC 0.64, P=0.012). The multivariable model demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.75. Based on the final multivariable regression model, a point-based instability risk score was derived to estimate patient-specific risk with good predictive accuracy. Conclusions Instability in C1 fractures was significantly associated with several factors including increasing lateral mass displacement, dens fracture, and neurologic deficit. These parameters outperformed legacy assessment tools based on radiographic measurement. Our prognostic utility demonstrated improved predictive performance and may assist clinicians in risk stratification and treatment decision-making.

title: Anterior Lumbar Plexus Position on Preoperative Supine MRI Is Associated With Postoperative Motor Deficits After Lateral Lumbar Interbody Fusion at L4-5.
abstract: Study design Retrospective propensity score-matched case-control study. Objective To evaluate whether preoperative MRI-based psoas morphology, lumbar plexus position, iliac crest height, and psoas cross-sectional area (CSA) are associated with postoperative motor deficits (PMDs) following standalone lateral lumbar interbody fusion (SA-LLIF) at L4-L5. Summary of background data PMDs remain a recognized complication of LLIF. Although anatomical characteristics have been implicated in neurological risk, the clinical value of classifying these features on preoperative MRI remains incompletely understood. Methods Patients who developed PMDs after L4-L5 SA-LLIF were propensity score matched to patients without PMDs. Preoperative supine MRI was used to assess operative-side psoas morphology (Amaral classification), lumbar plexus position (Moro zones), iliac crest height, and absolute and height-adjusted psoas CSA. Conditional logistic regression analyses, including a multivariable model incorporating both psoas morphology and lumbar plexus position, were performed to evaluate their associations with PMDs. Results A total of 172 matched patients were included. An anterior lumbar plexus position extending beyond the midpoint of the vertebral body on preoperative supine MRI (Moro Zones 1-2) remained independently associated with PMDs after adjustment for psoas morphology (OR 14.37, 95% CI 1.78-115.95; P=0.012). Although Type III psoas morphology according to the Amaral classification was associated with increased odds of PMDs in univariable analysis (OR 4.77, 95% CI 1.65-13.76; P=0.004), this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for lumbar plexus position (OR 2.54, 95% CI 0.90-7.18; P=0.078). Iliac crest height, psoas CSA, and height-adjusted psoas CSA were not associated with PMDs. Conclusions Psoas morphology and lumbar plexus position on preoperative supine MRI were associated with PMDs following L4-L5 SA-LLIF. An anterior lumbar plexus position remained independently associated with PMDs after adjustment for psoas morphology. These findings support preoperative MRI-based anatomical assessment for neurological risk stratification and patient counseling.

title: OPLL Is Associated With a CT-Defined Fracture/Dislocation-Free Injury Phenotype but Not AIS-Grade Conversion in Elderly Cervical Spinal Cord Injury.
abstract: Study design Retrospective multicenter cohort study. Objective To determine whether ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament (OPLL) identifies a CT-defined fracture/dislocation-free injury phenotype in older patients with traumatic cervical spinal cord injury (SCI), whether midsagittal canal occupancy reflects admission neurological severity, and whether OPLL predicts AIS-grade conversion. Summary of background data OPLL is considered a structural substrate for cervical cord injury without bony failure after trauma. However, its roles as an injury-pattern marker, severity metric, and recovery predictor remain unclear. Methods We analyzed 328 patients aged ≥65 years with traumatic cervical SCI from a 7-center registry. OPLL was present in 117 (36%) and classified on CT by subtype. CT-defined fracture/dislocation-free injury was the mechanistic endpoint, and ≥1-grade AIS improvement the functional endpoint. Multivariable logistic regression, multiple imputation, and center-level and energy-stratified sensitivity analyses were performed. Results OPLL-positive patients more often had fracture/dislocation-free injury (83% vs. 69%; adjusted OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.01-4.01). Retrospective multicenter cohort study.

To determine whether ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament (OPLL) identifies a CT-defined fracture/dislocation-free injury phenotype in older patients with traumatic cervical spinal cord injury (SCI), whether midsagittal canal occupancy reflects admission neurological severity, and whether OPLL predicts AIS-grade conversion.

title: Primary resistant disease is clinically heterogeneous in metastatic renal cell carcinoma treated with nivolumab plus ipilimumab.
abstract: The study aimed to characterize clinical heterogeneity among patients with primary resistant disease (PRD) after first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab (NIVO+IPI) for metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) and to explore clinical factors associated with death within 1 year among patients with PRD. We retrospectively analyzed 151 patients with mRCC who received first-line NIVO+IPI at four institutions in Japan between May 2018 and January 2025. PRD was defined as disease progression occurring within 3 months after treatment initiation, based on radiographic and clinical assessment, or death from any cause within the same period. For exploratory analyses, primary resistant disease with early mortality (PRD-EM) was defined as death within 1 year among patients with PRD. Survival was estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method. Because the PRD subgroup was small and several variables had sparse cell counts, associations with PRD-EM were assessed using Firth penalized logistic regression. PRD occurred in 31 of 151 patients (20.5%). Median overall survival was 3.9 months [95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.8-13.6] in patients with PRD and 46.7 months (95% CI = 38.8-62.8) in those without PRD (log-rank P < 0.001). Among patients with PRD, 20 of 31 (64.5%) met the exploratory PRD-EM definition. In the parsimonious two-variable Firth model, baseline C-reactive protein (CRP) ≥2 mg/dL [adjusted odds ratio (OR) = 7.95; 95% CI = 1.32-68.18; P = 0.023] and lymph node involvement (adjusted OR = 11.65; 95% CI = 1.78-142.82; P = 0.009) were associated with PRD-EM. PRD after first-line NIVO+IPI was associated with heterogeneous clinical outcomes. Elevated baseline CRP and lymph node involvement were associated with PRD-EM in an exploratory analysis. The PRD-EM classification and these associations require validation in larger independent cohorts before they can be used for clinical decision-making.

title: Diagnostic Performance of the Radiographic Assessment of Lung Edema Score for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome-Post Hoc Analysis of the "Validating Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers for Diagnosis" Study.
abstract: Objectives To determine the diagnostic accuracy of the Radiographic Assessment of Lung Edema (RALE) score for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and its interobserver reliability. Design Post hoc analysis of a prospective observational cohort study. Setting ICUs at Vanderbilt University Medical Center participating in the Validating Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers for Diagnosis study. Patients Adult patients receiving invasive ventilation for at least two consecutive days, with chest radiographs available on the first 2 ICU days. Interventions None. Measurements and main results Chest radiographs from the first 2 ICU days were scored independently by at least two experienced raters; scores were averaged per radiograph, and the highest averaged score from ICU day 1 or 2 was selected for analysis. The primary outcome was ARDS according to the Berlin definition during the first 2 ICU days. Of 236 patients, 92 (39%) had ARDS. The median RALE score was higher in patients with ARDS than in those without (29.5 [22.2-34.5] vs. 12.2 [7.5-17.8]; p < 0.01). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.93 (95% CI, 0.90-0.96). At the optimal cutoff of 20, sensitivity was 85%, specificity 83%, positive predictive value 76%, and negative predictive value 90%. Interobserver reliability was high, with pairwise intraclass correlation coefficients ranging from 0.81 to 0.87. Conclusions In patients invasively ventilated for at least 2 days, the RALE score demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy for ARDS at a cutoff of 20, together with high interobserver reliability, supporting its potential role as a standardized radiographic tool in the diagnosis of ARDS.

title: Comprehensive role of fluorine-18-labeled fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography across the disease course of primary malignant melanoma of the esophagus.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical value of fluorine-18-labeled fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET/computed tomography (CT) in managing primary malignant melanoma of the esophagus (PMME). Seventy patients with pathologically confirmed PMME between September 2011 and June 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The diagnostic performance of 18F-FDG PET/CT was analyzed for evaluating primary tumors, lymph nodes, recurrence, metastasis, and its role in predicting treatment response. Among 20 patients who underwent preoperative evaluation, no significant differences in 18F-FDG uptake or tumor wall thickness were observed between T1 and T2/T3 tumors (all P > 0.05). Lesion-based analysis revealed that the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for lymph node evaluation was 0.923 for 18F-FDG PET/CT and 0.738 for contrast-enhanced CT, with sensitivities of 82.6 and 47.8%, and specificities of 98.0 and 97.0%, respectively. Among 25 patients who received nonsurgical treatment, significant differences were found in maximum standardized uptake value, metabolic tumor volume (MTV), total lesion glycolysis (TLG), and tumor wall thickness between responders and nonresponders (all P < 0.05). Multivariate analysis identified TLG as an independent predictor of treatment response (odds ratio = 0.950, P = 0.025). In 50 patients evaluated for distant metastases and postoperative recurrence, additional findings from 18F-FDG PET/CT led to significant management changes in 14.0% of patients (7/50). 18F-FDG PET/CT is highly effective for evaluating lymph nodes and distant metastases in PMME, and facilitates early identification of patients likely to respond to treatment. It may serve as a valuable tool for staging, response prediction, and follow-up of patients with PMME.

title: BRAF wild-type metastatic melanoma arising in a congenital melanocytic nevus initially reported as melanoma in situ, 4 years after negative sentinel lymph node biopsy: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Melanoma arising in a congenital melanocytic nevus is uncommon, and distant relapse years after a thin primary tumor and a negative sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) is rarely documented in detail. A 34-year-old man underwent wide local excision of a bleeding congenital hairy nevus of the sacral skin. Histopathology showed melanoma in situ with a thin invasive component (<0.8 mm, nonulcerated, mitotic rate 7/10 high-power fields; recorded as pT1b), and BRAF testing was negative. After referral 2 years later, lymphoscintigraphy-guided SLNB was negative in all eight nodes from both groins and the right axilla. Four years after nodal staging, he presented with back pain, lower-limb weakness, and urinary retention from multiple vertebral metastases with an epidural component at L3, raising concern for cauda equina compression, together with solitary hepatic and pulmonary lesions, a pattern consistent with hematogenous dissemination. Liver and vertebral biopsies confirmed metastatic melanoma. Next-generation sequencing identified no variant of therapeutic or prognostic significance (BRAF wild-type) and a low tumor mutational burden (2.84 mutations/Mb). Palliative radiotherapy to L1-L4 (20 Gy in five fractions) restored ambulation, and denosumab and ipilimumab plus nivolumab, an accepted first-line option for BRAF wild-type melanoma, were started. In a lesion reported as melanoma in situ, the invasive component, not the in-situ component, confers metastatic potential. A negative SLNB does not exclude occult nodal disease or hematogenous dissemination. New skeletal or neurological symptoms in melanoma survivors warrant prompt imaging, even after a prolonged disease-free interval.
