title: Dynamic Cerebral Perfusion CT Imaging via a Low-Dimensional Manifold Model.
abstract: Dynamic cerebral perfusion computed tomography (DCPCT) enables the assessment of cerebral blood circulation and is therefore widely applied to cerebrovascular diseases diagnosis. However, the scanning protocol of this imaging technique significantly elevates the radiation exposure dose for patients. While decreasing the x-ray tube current directly reduces the radiation dose, the correspondingly increased quantum noise in projection data will severely degrade the quality of DCPCT images reconstructed using the classical filtered back-projection (FBP) algorithm. To enhance the image quality of DCPCT under low-dose scenarios, this study presents a statistical iterative reconstruction method based on the penalized weighted least-squares (PWLS) criterion, with a low-dimensional manifold model (LDMM) for regularization, called PWLS-LDMM. This approach leverages the observation that DCPCT images exhibit low-dimensional structure in their patch manifolds. By incorporating the dimension of these patch manifolds as regularization constraints into the image reconstruction process, subtle structural features can be effectively preserved in low-dose DCPCT images. We further developed an efficient alternating optimization algorithm to minimize the PWLS-LDMM objective function. In the experiments, a digital brain perfusion phantom and patient data were utilized to perform a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative assessment of the PWLS-LDMM method. The results show that compared to several representative model-based reconstruction methods, the presented PWLS-LDMM method exhibits significant advantages in noise reduction, artifact suppression, and structural detail preservation. Moreover, the DCPCT images reconstructed with this approach yield more precise cerebral hemodynamic parameter maps, providing reliable support for downstream clinical applications.

title: Boundary-Guided Mammographic Radiomics for Molecular Subtype Risk Stratification in Breast Cancer.
abstract: This work proposes a multi-stage interpretable framework for mammography-based molecular subtype-oriented risk stratification in breast cancer, focusing on visible mass lesions with segmentable tumor boundaries. The framework integrates a Boundary-Enhanced module within an attention-based U-Net architecture to improve tumor boundary delineation. Morphological and radiomics descriptors capturing shape, margin-related geometry, intensity, and texture heterogeneity are then extracted from the segmented tumor region and used for machine-learning-based subtype-oriented classification. For this task, the best-performing CatBoost model achieved an ROC AUC of 94.6% on Dataset A and 93.7% on Dataset B, used as an external test cohort for downstream subtype classification. These findings suggest that boundary-guided mammographic radiomics may provide a non-invasive adjunct for pre-biopsy risk stratification and subtype-oriented clinical assessment. However, tissue-based pathological evaluation remains the reference standard for definitive molecular subtype determination.

title: FocFormer-UNet: UNet With Focal Modulation and Transformers for Ultrasound Needle Tracking Using Photoacoustic Ground Truth.
abstract: Objective Ultrasound (US)-guided needle tracking is a critical procedure for various clinical diagnoses and treatment planning, highlighting the need for improved visualization methods to enhance accuracy. While deep learning (DL) techniques have been employed to boost needle visibility in US images, they often rely heavily on manual annotations or simulated datasets, which can introduce biases and limit real-world applicability. Photoacoustic (PA) imaging, known for its high contrast capabilities, offers a promising solution by providing superior needle visualization compared to conventional US images. Methods In this work, we present FocFormer-UNet, a DL network that leverages PA images of the needle as ground truth for training, eliminating the need for manual annotations. This approach significantly improves needle localization accuracy in US images, reducing the reliance on time-consuming manual labeling. Results FocFormer-UNet achieves excellent needle localization accuracy, demonstrated by a modified Hausdorff distance of 1.43$\pm$ 1.23 and a targeting error of 1.22$\pm$ 1.14 on human clinical dataset, indicating minimal deviation from actual needle positions. Conclusion Our method offers robust needle tracking across diverse US systems, improving the precision and reliability of US-guided needle insertion procedures. It holds great promise for advancing AI-driven clinical support tools in medical imaging.

title: Segment Anything Model 2: An Application to 2D and 3D Medical Images.
abstract: Segment Anything Model (SAM) has gained significant attention because of its ability to segment a variety of objects in images upon providing a prompt. Recently developed SAM 2 has extended this ability to video segmentation, and by substituting the third spatial dimension in 3D images for the time dimension in videos, it opens an opportunity to apply SAM 2 to 3D medical images. In this paper, we extensively evaluate SAM 2's ability to segment both 2D and 3D medical images using 80 prompt strategies across 21 medical imaging datasets, including 2D modalities (X-ray and ultrasound), 3D modalities (magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, and positron emission tomography), and surgical videos. We find that in the 2D setting, SAM 2 performs similarly to SAM, while in the 3D setting we observe that: (1) selecting the first mask is more effective than choosing the one with the highest confidence, (2) prompting the slice with the largest object appears is the most cost-effective strategy when only one slice is prompted, (3) box prompts result in higher performance than point prompts at a slightly higher annotation cost, (4) bidirectional propagation outperforms front-to-end propagation, (5) interactive annotation is rarely effective, (6) SAM 2, without fine-tuning, achieves 3D IoU from 0.32 with a single point prompt to 0.51 with a ground truth mask on one slice, and exceeds 0.8 on certain datasets when using box or ground-truth prompts, a level that begins to approach clinical usefulness. These findings demonstrate that SAM 2's ability to segment 3D medical images can be improved with our proposed strategies over the default ones, providing practical guidance for using SAM 2 for prompt-based 3D medical image segmentation.

title: PINN-EM: Physics-Guided Disease Progression Model of Geographic Atrophy.
abstract: Objective To construct a personalizable spatio-temporal disease progression model of patients with a late dry form of Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD), known as Geographic Atrophy (GA). Methods From a series of retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans, we infer the coefficients for the parametrized partial differential equation (PDE), such that the parametrized PDE best describes the observed imaging data. Acting as a soft constraint, the recovered PDE helps to extrapolate an implicit neural representation (INR) of the GA segmentation map progression. To enable efficient training, we propose an iterative method - PINN-EM, designed to recover coefficients of non-linear PDEs. At each iteration, the method decouples the problem into PDE coefficients fitting and data fitting steps, resembling Expectation Maximization algorithm. Results We extensively tested the proposed method in large-scale experiments using the open-source PDEBench benchmark to validate its performance. Furthermore, we applied the method to the challenging problem of GA progression modeling, where patients exhibit a high variance in GA growth patterns and speed. The proposed spatio-temporal disease progression model outperformed the baselines, even outperforming posterior knowledge models in Dice score for newly affected growth areas. Conclusion We demonstrated that the proposed spatio-temporal disease progression model fitted with introduced PINN-EM outperforms existing baselines in synthetic and real clinical applications, highlighting the extrapolation capabilities of the INR models. Significance The proposed spatio-temporal disease progression model and PINN-EM fitting procedure can be applied across diverse domains facing the challenge of fitting parametrized PDE to the empirical datasets.

Objective

To construct a personalizable spatio-temporal disease progression model of patients with a late dry form of Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD), known as Geographic Atrophy (GA).

Methods

From a series of retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans, we infer the coefficients for the parametrized partial differential equation (PDE), such that the parametrized PDE best describes the observed imaging data. Acting as a soft constraint, the recovered PDE helps to extrapolate an implicit neural representation (INR) of the GA segmentation map progression. To enable efficient training, we propose an iterative method - PINN-EM, designed to recover coefficients of non-linear PDEs. At each iteration, the method decouples the problem into PDE coefficients fitting and data fitting steps, resembling Expectation Maximization algorithm.

Results

We extensively tested the proposed method in large-scale experiments using the open-source PDEBench benchmark to validate its performance. Furthermore, we applied the method to the challenging problem of GA progression modeling, where patients exhibit a high variance in GA growth patterns and speed. The proposed spatio-temporal disease progression model outperformed the baselines, even outperforming posterior knowledge models in Dice score for newly affected growth areas.

Conclusion

We demonstrated that the proposed spatio-temporal disease progression model fitted with introduced PINN-EM outperforms existing baselines in synthetic and real clinical applications, highlighting the extrapolation capabilities of the INR models.

Significance

The proposed spatio-temporal disease progression model and PINN-EM fitting procedure can be applied across diverse domains facing the challenge of fitting parametrized PDE to the empirical datasets.

title: LDiT3D: Head and Neck Tumor Segmentation Using a 3D Latent Diffusion Transformer Model.
abstract: Objective Head and neck (H&N) tumors are among the most common cancers worldwide. However, manual annotation of H&N tumors for each patient poses a significant burden on clinicians. Therefore, developing automated and accurate methods for H&N tumor segmentation is of great clinical importance. Methods We introduce LDiT3D, a novel 3D transformer-based diffusion model designed to segment H&N tumors from 3D Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and X-ray computed tomography (CT) scans, primarily focusing on oropharyngeal tumors. LDiT3D utilizes stacked 3D vision transformer blocks to effectively capture spatial context in volumetric data. To address the high computational cost typically associated with 3D transformers, we incorporate a pre-trained autoencoder that projects the input into a lower-dimensional latent space where the diffusion process is performed more efficiently. In addition to the diffusion loss computed in latent space, a task-specific segmentation loss is introduced in pixel space to further enhance segmentation accuracy. Results Methods based on U-Net and transformer architectures were selected as reference methods. Comparative results demonstrated that the proposed LDiT3D achieved highly accurate segmentation performance, with the highest Dice Score and lowest Hausdorff distance on both public and local datasets. Moreover, LDiT3D showed a more balanced performance between Precision and Recall, as indicated by the highest Fowlkes-Mallows Score. Ablation studies further confirmed the effectiveness of the key components in the LDiT3D design. Conclusion LDiT3D delivers more accurate and balanced H&N tumor segmentation compared to reference methods. Significance These findings highlight LDiT3D's potential to improve automated H&N tumor annotation and advance medical image analysis.

title: DPSeg: Differentiated Perception Medical Image Segmentation via Context-Aware Compensation and Stratified Uncertainty Attention.
abstract: In medical image segmentation, accurate recognition of regions hindered by blurry boundaries, low contrast, and complex backgrounds is crucial. These issues lead to significant differences in segmentation difficulty within a single image. However, existing methods typically adopt a uniform modeling strategy across the entire feature map, overlooking the mismatch between segmentation difficulty and attention intensity. Consequently, they fail to adequately focus on key regions, diluting the representations of challenging regions. To address these challenges, we propose DPSeg, a differentiated perception medical image segmentation framework via context-aware compensation and stratified uncertainty attention. Specifically, DPSeg comprises three key components. The Context-Aware Compensation (CAC) module refines encoder features by integrating key region-aware prompts and contextual information, compensating for encoding-induced distortions and enabling differentiated perception, thereby providing higher-quality representations for decoding. Additionally, the Stratified Uncertainty Transformer (SUTrans) module explicitly modulates the attention intensity of different regions based on their segmentation uncertainty, thereby possessing differentiated perception ability while effectively suppressing redundant feature interactions. Moreover, we propose a Foreground-Uncertainty Adaptive Weighted Loss (FUAWL) to enable differentiated supervision across decoding stages, applying stronger guidance to uncertain regions in shallow decoding and emphasizing foreground regions in deep decoding to improve boundary delineation and mitigate foreground-background imbalance. Extensive experiments on four challenging datasets demonstrate that DPSeg achieves competitive segmentation performance.

title: Autoregressive Generative Medical Image Segmentation.
abstract: Recent years have witnessed rapid progress in deep learning-based medical image segmentation. Existing approaches can be broadly categorized into discriminative models, which formulate segmentation as a pixel-wise classification problem, and generative models, which treat segmentation as a image conditioned mask generation task. While discriminative models often achieve strong performance on in-distribution data, they tend to generalize poorly under domain shifts. In contrast, generative models exhibit stronger generalization by modeling the joint distribution of images and labels, but often sacrifice fine-grained boundary accuracy due to limited sensitivity to local structural details. In this work, we propose AutoRegressive Generative Medical Image Segmentation (ARGMS), a unified framework that formulates segmentation as a coarse-to-fine, image-conditioned autoregressive mask generation process. ARGMS leverages a pretrained vision foundation model to project both images and labels into a shared latent space, and progressively generates multi-scale label representations via a causal Transformer. To bridge the semantic gap between image and label representations, we introduce a Spatial-Channel Feature Aggregation (SCFA) module that provides semantically informative conditioning signals throughout the generation process. Furthermore, we design a Conjunction Adversarial Network (CAN) to perform multi-scale latent alignment and rejection-based inference, effectively mitigating error accumulation during autoregressive decoding. By integrating multi-scale label generation, latent-space alignment, and adversarial consistency constraints, ARGMS achieves accurate and structurally coherent segmentation across diverse datasets. Extensive experiments on five public benchmarks demonstrate that ARGMS consistently outperforms both discriminative and generative baselines, while exhibiting strong generalization and scalability across different imaging modalities and dataset scales.

title: ZonoSeg: A Zonal-aware Prostate Segmentation Framework on 3D MRI images.
abstract: Accurate zonal-aware prostate segmentation in clinical 3D MRI is important for diagnosis and treatment planning. However, delineating the central-gland-peripheral-zone interface remains challenging because gradual tissue transitions, irregular internal boundaries, and pathology-induced appearance variations can lead to clinically relevant zonal boundary errors. We propose ZonoSeg, a hierarchical encoder-decoder framework that targets these ambiguous boundaries via uncertainty-aware, boundary-sensitive feature transmission in stage-wise skip connections. The ZonoSeg Block combines edge cues with learnable multi-scale Gaussian smoothing to construct a continuous probabilistic boundary field, and the ZAD head further refines zonal separation through explicit foreground-background interactions. Experiments demonstrate improved boundary localization and robust zonal segmentation on both dual-target and single-target tasks across eight multi-center prostate MRI datasets; on PROMISE MRI BMC, ZonoSeg achieves Dice scores of 83.39% for the central gland and 84.10% for the peripheral zone, with HD95 of 3.84 mm and 3.41 mm, respectively. Code: https://github.com/deepang-ai/ZonoSeg.

title: Decoupling Multi-Contrast Super-Resolution: Self-Supervised Implicit Re-Representation for Unpaired Cross-Modal Synthesis.
abstract: Multi-contrast super-resolution (MCSR) is crucial for enhancing MRI but current deep learning methods are limited. They typically require large, paired low- and high-resolution (LR/HR) training datasets, which are scarce, and are trained for fixed upsampling scales. While recent self-supervised methods remove the paired data requirement, they fail to leverage valuable population-level priors. In this work, we propose a novel, decoupled MCSR framework that resolves both limitations. We reformulate MCSR into two stages: (1) an unpaired cross-modal synthesis (uCMS) module, trained once on unpaired population data to learn a robust anatomical prior; and (2) a lightweight, patient-specific implicit re-representation (IrR) module. This IrR module is optimized in a self-supervised manner to fuse the population prior with the subject's own LR target data. This design uniquely fuses population-level knowledge with patient-specific fidelity without requiring paired target-domain LR/HR training data or paired cross-modal HR reference-target training data. Here, 'unpaired' refers to the population-level training setting; at subject-specific inference, as in standard MCSR, the method uses a matched HR reference image from another contrast together with the subject's LR target image. By building the IrR module on an implicit neural representation, our framework is also inherently scale-agnostic. Our method demonstrates superior quantitative performance on different datasets, with exceptional robustness at extreme scales (16×, 32×), a regime where competing methods fail. Our work presents a data-efficient, flexible, and computationally lightweight paradigm for MCSR, enabling high-fidelity, arbitrary-scale reconstruction without the need for paired population-level supervision.

title: EM-SliceCrafter: Distilling Lightweight 2D CNNs for Efficient 3D EM Neuron Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate 3D neuron segmentation from large-scale electron microscopy (EM) volumes is a cornerstone of connectomics, yet it is hampered by a trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency. While 3D Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) offer high accuracy by predicting 3D affinity maps, their high computational cost and limited input size impede their application to large-scale data. To overcome this, we introduce EM-SliceCrafter, a novel framework that employs a lightweight 2D CNN for both efficient and precise 3D neuron segmentation. Our method generates a 3D affinity map by computing distances between embedding maps of adjacent 2D slices. To enrich the 2D network's contextual understanding, we propose a dual-distillation strategy. First, Cross-Dimension Affinity Distillation (CAD) transfers inter-slice structural knowledge from a 3D teacher network to enhance 3D continuity. Complementarily, Internal-Dimension Affinity Distillation (IAD) leverages a powerful teacher built on the pre-trained Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) encoder, using a learnable adapter, to distill fine-grained intra-slice boundary details. Furthermore, a Feature Grafting Interaction (FGI) module deepens knowledge transfer by integrating embeddings across the student and both teacher networks. Extensive experiments on diverse EM datasets, featuring various imaging modalities and resolutions, show that EM-SliceCrafter improves segmentation accuracy over state-of-the-art methods while achieving a 33× speedup in GPU forward inference. The code is available at https://github.com/liuxy1103/EM-SliceCrafter.

title: Multiparameter Uncertainty Mapping in Quantitative Molecular MRI using a Physics-Structured Variational Autoencoder (PS-VAE).
abstract: Quantitative imaging methods, such as magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF), aim to extract interpretable pathology biomarkers by estimating biophysical tissue parameters from signal evolutions. However, the pattern-matching algorithms or neural networks used in such inverse problems often lack principled uncertainty quantification, which limits the trustworthiness and transparency, required for clinical acceptance. Here, we describe a physics-structured variational autoencoder (PS-VAE) designed for rapid extraction of voxelwise multi-parameter posterior distributions. Our approach integrates a differentiable spin physics simulator with self-supervised learning, and provides a full covariance that captures the inter-parameter correlations in the latent biophysical space. The method was validated in a multi-proton pool chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) and semisolid magnetization transfer (MT) molecular MRF study, across in-vitro phantoms, tumor-bearing mice, healthy human volunteers, and subjects with glioblastoma and Alzheimer's Disease. The resulting multi-parametric posteriors are in good agreement with those calculated using a brute-force Bayesian analysis, while providing an orders-of-magnitude acceleration in whole brain quantification. In addition, we demonstrate how monitoring the multi-parameter posterior dynamics across progressively acquired signals provides practical insights for protocol optimization and may facilitate real-time adaptive acquisition. The code and sample data are available at https://github.com/momentum-laboratory/ps-vae.

title: EyeGraph: A Multi-granularity Medical Vision-Language Foundation Model with Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Ophthalmic Interpretation.
abstract: The exponential growth of large vision-language models (VLMs) has created significant opportunities for advancing multimodal artificial intelligence in specialized domains such as ophthalmology. However, progress in ophthalmic VLMs remains limited, primarily due to the lack of large-scale, high-quality image-text pairs. Moreover, existing VLMs frequently generate hallucinations, leading to uncertainty and unreliability that are unacceptable in clinical practice. To address the data scarcity issue, we introduce IT-Retinal, a dedicated ophthalmic Vision Question Answering (VQA) dataset that providesmultigranularity tasks and high-quality long-form textual content in image-text pairs. To mitigate hallucinations, we propose EyeGraph, a framework for ophthalmic VLMs that consists of two training stages, targeted pre-training and fine-tuning, and one inference stage that integrates Graph of Thought (GoT) and Think on Graph (ToG) reasoning, referred to as G2T. This design enables EyeGraph to incorporate structured external knowledge, constrain the output space, and produce more clinically consistent results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EyeGraph achieves state-of-the-art performance across seven clinically relevant benchmarks, spanning disease diagnosis, structural detection and localization, and report generation. Notably, the proposed G2T reasoning module consistently improves the factual consistency and reliability of ophthalmic report generation. All source code, along with an interactive demo, is publicly available at: https://github.com/ZardCAI/EyeGraph.

title: Latent Interpolation Learning Using Diffusion Models for Cardiac Volume Reconstruction.
abstract: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) imaging is a critical tool for diagnosing and managing cardiovascular disease, yet its utility is often limited by the sparse acquisition of 2D short-axis slices, resulting in incomplete volumetric information. Accurate 3D reconstruction from these sparse slices is essential for comprehensive cardiac assessment, but existing methods face challenges, including reliance on predefined interpolation schemes (e.g., linear or spherical), computational inefficiency, and dependence on additional semantic inputs such as segmentation labels or motion data. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Cardiac Latent Interpolation Diffusion (CaLID) framework that introduces three key innovations. First, we present a data-driven interpolation scheme based on diffusion models, which can capture complex, non-linear relationships between sparse slices and improves reconstruction accuracy. Second, we design a computationally efficient method that operates in the latent space and speeds up generative 3D whole-heart upsampling time by a factor of 24, reducing computational overhead compared to previous methods. Third, with only sparse 2D CMR images as input, our method achieves SOTA performance against baseline methods, eliminating the need for auxiliary input such as morphological guidance, thus simplifying workflows. We further extend our method to 2D+T data, enabling the effective modeling of spatiotemporal dynamics and ensuring temporal coherence. Extensive volumetric evaluations and downstream segmentation tasks demonstrate that CaLID achieves superior reconstruction quality and efficiency. By addressing the fundamental limitations of existing approaches, our framework advances the state of the art for spatio and spatiotemporal whole-heart reconstruction, offering a robust and clinically practical solution for cardiovascular imaging. The code is available at https://github.com/niklasbubeck/calid.

title: PARDA: A Perceive-Act-Reflect-Distill Agent for Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation.
abstract: Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (SFUDA) has emerged as a critical paradigm for addressing severe domain shifts in medical image segmentation under strict data privacy constraints, where source data are inaccessible. However, existing SFUDA methods primarily rely on static, open-loop adaptation pipelines, lacking the ability to actively perceive target domain characteristics and use reflection to correct accumulated errors. Meanwhile, Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) and Vision Language Models (VLMs) exhibit strong generalization across modalities and anatomies, yet their high computational inference overhead and deployment constraints prevent direct adoption on clinical edge devices. In this work, we propose PARDA, a VLM-coupled closed-loop SFUDA framework for medical image segmentation. PARDA reformulates SFUDA as a closed-loop decision-making process, in which the method actively perceives target domain characteristics, acts by coordinating semantic and geometric VFMs to generate pseudo-labels, reflects on the reliability of its anatomical and structural representations to guide refinement, and finally distills the acquired adaptation knowledge into a lightweight student model. This design enables PARDA to mitigate error accumulation while preserving data privacy and inference efficiency. We conduct a comprehensive SFUDA evaluation covering 13 cross-modality domain adaptation directions and 24 anatomical targets across diverse organs and imaging modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that PARDA achieves robust and universal domain adaptation while distilling the adaptation results into a lightweight student model for resource-constrained inference.

title: Noise2Match: Self-Supervised Low-Dose CT Denoising via Adaptive Inter-Slice Matching.
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning, supervised convolutional neural network methods have greatly improved the performance of low-dose computed tomography (CT) denoising. However, they require paired noisy-clean training data, which is difficult to obtain in practice. Some classic self-supervised denoising methods rely on the assumption of pixel-wise independent noise, making them ineffective for correlated noise in low-dose CT (LDCT) images. Considering the high similarity and weaker noise correlation between adjacent CT slices, several recently proposed self-supervised methods use adjacent LDCT slices for training. Nevertheless, these approaches fail to effectively account for the non-rigid mis-alignment between slices caused by anatomical variation, hindering them from satisfying the equal-mean condition required by the classic Noise2Noise framework. In this paper, we propose Noise2Match, a self-supervised LDCT denoising method based on adaptive inter-slice matching. Noise2Match introduces an inter-slice matching network to model the label transition process between adjacent slices, and then applies correction to the denoiser's outputs to better satisfy the equal-mean condition. We theoretically prove that, under idealized conditions, training Noise2Match using adjacent LDCT slices is equivalent to supervised training with paired noisy-clean images. We further find that Noise2Match can also effectively perform low-dose cone-beam CT (CBCT) denoising, which could be attributed to its correction operation that reduces inter-slice noise correlation. To the best of our knowledge, Noise2Match is the first effective image-domain self-supervised method for low-dose CBCT. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Noise2Match outperforms existing image-domain self-supervised methods, offering broader applicability and higher practical value.

title: Stochastic Siamese MAE Pretraining for Longitudinal Medical Images.
abstract: Temporally aware image representations are crucial for capturing disease progression in 3D volumes of longitudinal medical datasets. However, recent state-of-the-art self-supervised learning approaches like Masked Autoencoding (MAE), despite their strong representation learning capabilities, lack temporal awareness. In this paper, we propose STAMP (Stochastic Temporal Autoencoder with Masked Pretraining), a Siamese MAE framework that encodes temporal information through a stochastic process by conditioning on the time difference between the 2 input volumes. Unlike deterministic Siamese approaches, which compare scans from different time points but fail to account for the inherent uncertainty in disease evolution, STAMP learns temporal dynamics stochastically by reframing the MAE reconstruction loss as a conditional variational inference objective. We evaluated STAMP on two OCT and one MRI datasets with multiple visits per patient. STAMP pretrained ViT models outperformed both existing temporal MAE methods and foundation models on different late stage Age-Related Macular Degeneration and Alzheimer's Disease progression prediction which require models to learn the underlying non-deterministic temporal dynamics of the diseases.

title: DuMeta++: Spatiotemporal Dual Meta-Learning for Generalizable Few-Shot Brain Tissue Segmentation Across Diverse Ages.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of brain tissues from MRI scans is critical for neuroscience and clinical applications, but achieving consistent performance across the human lifespan remains challenging due to dynamic, age-related changes in brain appearance and morphology. While prior work has sought to mitigate these shifts by using self-supervised regularization with paired longitudinal data, such data are often unavailable in practice. To address this, we propose DuMeta++, a dual meta-learning framework that operates without paired longitudinal data. Our approach integrates: (1) meta-feature learning to extract age-agnostic semantic representations of spatiotemporally evolving brain structures, and (2) meta-initialization learning to enable data-efficient adaptation of the segmentation model. Furthermore, we propose a memory-bank-based class-aware regularization strategy to enforce longitudinal consistency without explicit longitudinal super-vision. We further characterize the convergence of the dual meta-learning pipeline under standard smoothness assumptions. Extensive experiments on the iSeg-2019 and ADNI datasets under one- and five-shot settings demonstrate that DuMeta++ consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both segmentation accuracy and longitudinal consistency. Code will be available at https:// github.com/ladderlab-xjtu/DuMeta++.

title: Tomographic Sparse View Selection Using the View Covariance Loss.
abstract: Standard computed tomography (CT) reconstruction algorithms such as filtered back projection (FBP) and Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) require many views for producing high-quality reconstructions, which can slow image acquisition and increase cost in non-destructive evaluation (NDE) applications. Over the past 20 years, a variety of methods have been developed for computing high-quality CT reconstructions from sparse views. However, the problem of how to select the best views for CT reconstruction remains open. In this paper, we present a novel view covariance loss (VCL) function that measures the joint information of a set of views by approximating the normalized mean squared error (NMSE) of the reconstruction. We present fast algorithms for computing the VCL along with an algorithm for selecting a subset of views that approximately minimizes its value. Our experiments on simulated and measured data indicate that for a fixed number of views our proposed view covariance loss selection (VCLS) algorithm results in reconstructions with lower NRMSE, fewer artifacts, and greater accuracy than current alternative approaches.

title: Negation-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models.
abstract: In this paper, we study a practical but less-touched problem in Vision-Language Models (VLMs), i.e., negation understanding. Specifically, many real-world applications require models to explicitly identify what is false or non-existent, e.g., radiologists may search for images that exclude specific conditions. Despite the impressive transferability of VLMs through large-scale training, they suffer from a critical limitation that fails to handle negation. To address this challenge, existing methods attribute its root cause to the scarcity of negation training data and propose to fine-tune VLMs on massive data containing explicit negation. Undoubtedly, such data-centric solutions demand substantial data and computational resources, limiting their sustainable widespread adoption. To tackle negation in a low-carbon manner, we empirically observe that the key obstacle lies in the dual-concept shifts between the affirmation and negation distributions. Therefore, we propose a Negation-Aware Test-Time Adaptation (NEAT) method to efficiently adjust distribution-related parameters during inference. In brief, NEAT can reduce distribution shift in consistent semantics while eliminating false distributional consistency in unrelated semantics. Extensive experiments on the various negation understanding tasks verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Remarkably, with less than 0.01% of trainable parameters, NEAT achieves comparable or superior performance to state-of-the-art post-training approaches.

title: RAC-Net: Interpretable Medical Small Target Segmentation Network With X-Ray Radiation Attenuation Characterization.
abstract: Medical image target segmentation is critical for clinical diagnosis and treatment, yet mainstream methods perform poorly on small medical targets due to inefficient sparse feature extraction and severe background interference. To tackle this issue, we propose Radiation Attenuation Characteristics Network (RAC-Net) inspired by the X-ray attenuation physical prior in CT imaging, aiming to boost small target segmentation accuracy for early lesion detection and localization. Specifically, RAC-Net integrates two tailored innovative modules: the Radiation Attenuation Salient Feature Extraction (RASFE) module leverages X-ray attenuation principles to extract small target Gaussian saliency features and suppress background noise, enhancing sparse feature representation; the Partial Volume Artifact Edge Enhancement (PVA) module embedded with CT Hounsfield Unit value prior fuses learnable neighborhood weights and physical prior weights, alleviating feature distortion and edge blurring caused by partial volume artifacts, while improving model robustness via clinical medical priors. Extensive experiments validate that RAC-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance in medical small target segmentation, with 18% DICE and 19% IOU improvements over advanced existing methods, providing solid support for early disease diagnosis and intervention.

title: Towards Medical Image Dataset Distillation: A Progressive Trajectory Matching and Dynamic Diversity Enhancing Method.
abstract: Sharing medical image sets is essential yet challenging due to limited resource and strict regulatory, which significantly hinder the development of medical foundation models and the transfer of medical domain knowledge. In this paper, we utilize medical image dataset distillation techniques to enable effective model construction and knowledge transfer without requiring downstream users to directly access the original data. Trajectory matching has become the mainstream distillation technique, yet our empirical findings on medical image datasets reveal two critical phenomena: instability of distillation optimization and redundancy of synthetic images. To investigate these phenomena, we conduct a theoretical analysis from the perspectives of bi-level optimization and neural tangent kernel, and formally define them as two core challenges: trajectory matching drift and intra-class diversity decay, which underscore the need for more stable and diversity-preserving trajectory matching methods. Guided by the analysis results, we propose a novel progressive and diverse dataset distillation (PD$^{3}$) method, which incorporates (1) a progressive trajectory matching paradigm that progressively unrolls the student training trajectory to extend the matching horizon, while adaptively selecting optimal expert matching trajectory to ensure stable and convergent distillation optimization; and (2) a dynamic diversity enhancing module that alleviates the redundancy of synthetic images by enhancing intra-class distribution and breaking redundancy accumulation. To facilitate fair evaluation, we establish a comprehensive medical image dataset distillation benchmark covering diverse medical image modalities. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method achieves an average absolute improvement of 10.20% and a relative gain of 20.09% over prior state-of-the-art methods, highlighting its effectiveness and practical potential.

title: Rotation Equivariant Mamba for Vision Tasks.
abstract: Rotation equivariance is an important structural prior for a broad range of vision tasks, particularly in domains such as remote sensing and medical imaging where objects have no canonical orientation, yet it remains notably absent from current Mamba-based vision architectures. Despite the success of Mamba in natural language processing and its growing adoption in computer vision, existing visual Mamba models fail to account for rotational symmetry in their design. This omission renders them sensitive to image rotations, thereby constraining their robustness and cross-task generalization. To address this limitation, we incorporate rotation symmetry, an important geometric prior in many visual domains, into Mamba-based architectures. Specifically, we introduce EQ-VMamba, the first rotation equivariant visual Mamba architecture for vision tasks. The core components of EQ-VMamba include a carefully designed rotation equivariant cross-scan strategy and group Mamba blocks. Moreover, we provide a rigorous theoretical analysis of the intrinsic equivariance error, demonstrating that the proposed architecture enforces end-to-end rotation equivariance under the $\mathrm{p}4$ rotation group. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks-including high-level image classification, mid-level semantic segmentation, and low-level image super-resolution-demonstrate that EQ-VMamba consistently improves rotation robustness and achieves superior or competitive performance compared to non-equivariant baselines on most evaluated benchmarks, while requiring 40-70% fewer parameters. These results indicate that embedding rotation equivariance not only effectively bolsters the robustness of visual Mamba models against rotation transformations, but also improves accuracy on data exhibiting rotational symmetry, with substantially improved parameter efficiency.

title: Correlation of NEC to Image SNR and Lesion Detectability in clinical TOF PET.
abstract: In positron emission tomography (PET) imaging, Noise Equivalent Counts (NEC) serve as a key indicator of overall system performance. Previous studies have established the relationship between NEC and signal-to-noise (SNR) for both non-time-of-flight (non-TOF) and TOF PET scanners employing filtered back-projection (FBP) algorithms. This study aims to explore the correlation between NEC and image SNR, as well as task-specific metrics, using iterative reconstruction with comprehensive TOF PET system modeling. The phantom, 35 cm in diameter to represent a patient with high BMI, featured twelve 1-cm diameter spheres placed in an off centered slice, and data were acquired across a wide range of activity levels using the PennPET Explorer. Multiple scans were generated via bootstrapping and reconstructed using list-mode TOF-ordered subset expectation maximization (TOF-OSEM) algorithms to obtain mean and standard deviation images. Image SNR was quantified as the ratio of mean values within a central volume-of-interest (VOI) across both images. Utilizing a generalized scan-statistic model, the area under the localization receiver operating characteristic (ALROC) was calculated for the spheres placed at the offset slice. NEC was computed using both conventional and TOF-adapted formulas from the original data. The results indicate that while image SNR scales approximately linearly with NEC, this relationship becomes substantially more consistent when NEC TOF is used, demonstrating that NEC TOF is a better predictor of global image SNR under iterative reconstruction than conventional NEC. Furthermore, our results show that although ALROC is proportional to SNR, it does not adequately represent the change in ALROC as TOF resolution improves.

title: Intelligent Diagnosis of Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions Based on Endobronchial Ultrasound Images Using Multi-modal Features.
abstract: Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. For peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) that cannot be definitively diagnosed by computed tomography (CT) or positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) imaging, endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial lung biopsy (EBUS-TBLB) for pathological examinations still carries a significant possibility of indefinite diagnosis. Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) serves as not only a valuable and widely used guidance technique but also a superior diagnostic technique for PPLs compared with CT or PET-CT, by enabling direct visualization of the structures within the lesion and the echo distributions outside the lesion. Aimed at classifying PPLs as benign or malignant, this study enrolled 313 patients for the final analysis. Multi-modal features including clinical, radiomic, and deep features were integrated and fed into an artificial neural network for feature selection, fusion, and prediction based on the long-axis diameter of PPLs measured on CT images with a threshold of 3 cm. To reduce manual effort and maximize the diagnostic performance of multi-modal features, we employed the particle swarm optimization algorithm to automatically optimize the combination of selected features and model structure. Our method achieves an average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.981 (95% CI: 0.953-1.000), accuracy of 0.964, sensitivity of 0.963, specificity of 0.969, and F1-score of 0.976 on the independent test dataset after four-fold cross-validation. The outstanding diagnostic performance for PPLs based on EBUS images, with all the evaluation metrics exceeding 0.95, can provide a solid foundation for clinical decision-making, biopsy site selection, and follow-up observations.
authorString: Chen Z, Feng J, Wei X, Huang L, He Q, Li S, Zhong C, Luo J.

title: Compound Lens Design and Beamforming for Wide-Field Volumetric Imaging Using a Row-Column Array.
abstract: Row-column addressed (RCA) ultrasound arrays enable volumetric imaging with a significantly reduced channel count compared to fully addressed 2-D arrays; however, their field of view (FOV) is typically limited to the transducer footprint. Diverging acoustic lenses can extend the FOV, but accurate beamforming remains challenging when the lens's finite thickness and multilayer structure are not properly modeled. This work presents a compound acoustic lens design that simultaneously achieves a large FOV, reduced edge-wave artifacts, and acceptable sensitivity loss, together with a beamforming approach that accurately accounts for wave propagation through multilayer lens structures. The proposed approach combines ray tracing with a Normal Path (RT-NP) approximation and determines the optimal propagation path using a two-dimensional Newton-Raphson optimization, enabling accurate time-of-flight (TOF) estimation while significantly reducing computational complexity compared to conventional two-interface ray-tracing methods. The method is validated experimentally using a 128+128 Vermon RCA transducer operating at 6 MHz and equipped with a BiQuadratic compound lens composed of TPX and RTV-PTFE materials. Pressure-field measurements validate the predicted wavefront expansion, while simulations indicate an FOV expansion to approximately 54.5°, enabling imaging well beyond the transducer aperture while preserving high spatial resolution and image quality. Hydrophone and RF-data measurements demonstrate sub-wavelength TOF accuracy of the proposed beamformer. The proposed system achieves a penetration depth of 75 mm compared with 90 mm without the lens, with only minor degradation in spatial resolution. These results demonstrate that compound-lens RCA systems, combined with accurate and efficient beamforming, enable wide-field volumetric imaging of organ-scale structures while preserving the practical advantages of RCA arrays, with a theoretical volume rate of approximately 104 Hz, indicating the potential for real-time 3-D visualization.

title: Automated Volumetric ROI Selection for Ultrasound Attenuation-Based Assessment of Liver Steatosis.
abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) attenuation imaging is a promising low-cost approach for hepatic steatosis assessment, but current methods remain sensitive to operator-defined region-of-interest (ROI) selection and may not fully exploit volumetric acquisitions. We present an automated multi-plane attenuation-coefficient estimation (ACE) method for matrix-array ultrasound that defines and refines the attenuation ROI through learning-based liver masking, vessel exclusion, axial range detection, model-based Aline rejection, and robust plane aggregation. The method was tuned and tested in phantoms and subsequently evaluated against same-visit MRI proton-density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) in 35 subjects with 237 volumetric acquisitions. Subject-level ACE was defined as the median across repeated acquisitions, and repeatability was quantified using the within-subject coefficient of variation (CV). Subject-level ACE was associated with MRI-PDFF, yielding Pearson r = 0.8835 (95% CI, 0.8182-0.9349), Spearman ρ = 0.9135 (95% CI, 0.7926-0.9579), and R 2 = 0.7806. The mean within-subject CV was 3.24% (95% CI, 2.82-3.67%). AUCs were 0.958 (95% CI, 0.871-1.000) for distinguishing S1+ from S0 at MRI-PDFF ≥ 6% and 0.954 (95% CI, 0.878-1.000) for distinguishing S2+ from S0/S1 at MRI-PDFF ≥ 17%. These findings support the feasibility of an automated post-acquisition volumetric attenuation-imaging pipeline that reduces dependence on manual ROI selection for quantitative liver fat assessment.

title: Boiling Histotripsy with 1.1/3.3 MHz Dual-Frequency Inducing Long-Duration Anti-Tumor Immunity in Mice Breast Cancer.
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) has a poor prognosis and high risk of recurrence and metastasis. Histotripsy is an ultrasound-guided, non-invasive, non-thermal ablation method that mechanically lyses target tissues. A boiling histotripsy (DF-MS BH) technique combining 1.1/3.3 MHz superposition with a multi-stage ultrasound pulse scheme was proposed, aiming to enhance anti-tumor immune response by optimizing pulse dose and number of treatments. A custom-designed 1.1-/3.3-MHz two-element confocal-annular array and multi-stage ultrasound pulses were used for treatment. For 6-mm-diameter tumors, the ablated volume accounted for 60-70 % of the total tumor volume. The anti-tumor immune results showed increasing pulse dose from 85 to 115 elevated DAMPs release and reduced tumor growth rate. After the first high-dose pulse treatment, the infiltration level of CD8 + T cells gradually increased and then decreased on the 7th day, which contributed to a 9-day period of tumor growth arrest. Following the second treatment, the release of danger signals was further augmented. Meanwhile, the high-level infiltration of CD8 + T cells persisted for 35 days, extending the tumor growth arrest period to 25 days and prolonging the median survival period of mice to 50 days. In addition, this treatment strategy effectively reduced the number of lung metastases, confirming its ability to enhance systemic anti-tumor immune response. Furthermore, DF-MS BH ameliorated the immunosuppressive microenvironment of TNBC through first and second enhanced treatments. Ultimately, the combination therapy of DF-MS BH and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) further suppressed tumor recurrence and metastasis.

title: Diagnostic Utility of Full-Length BP180 and Native BP180-α6β4 Integrin Complex ELISAs in Serologically Inconclusive Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid.
abstract: Mucous membrane pemphigoid (MMP) is a chronic autoimmune subepithelial blistering disorder of mucosal surfaces that can cause irreversible scarring, blindness, or dysphagia. Early diagnosis is challenging because histopathology is nonspecific and conventional BP180 NC16A ELISAs have limited sensitivity. We evaluated ELISAs using full-length recombinant BP180 and a native BP180-α6β4 integrin complex in six patients with suspected oral or ocular MMP. The conventional NC16A ELISA was negative in four of six patients, and biopsy alone was often insufficient. Both assays provided useful serological support in a subset of cases when interpreted alongside direct immunofluorescence (DIF) and clinical phenotype, whereas in others DIF remained the primary basis for diagnosis. These assays can therefore complement, but not replace, clinicopathological assessment in suspected MMP.

title: Green Ultrasound-Assisted Extraction of Bioactive Phenolics From Quince (Cydonia oblonga) Leaves: Multi-Response Optimization, LC-MS/MS Profiling, and Comparison With Conventional Methods.
abstract: Quince (Cydonia oblonga Mill.) leaves are an abundant yet underutilized agricultural by-product that is rich in phenolic compounds and therefore represents a promising feedstock for value-added bioactive extracts. This study optimized the green ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) of bioactive compounds from quince leaves using a sequential statistical approach based on Plackett-Burman screening and Taguchi-based criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (CRITIC)-weighted grey relational analysis (GRA). Under the optimum conditions (solid-to-liquid ratio 3:50 g/mL, 50% (v/v) ethanol, and 75°C), the extract exhibited a total phenolic content (TPC) of 9210.44 ± 138.25 mg GAE L - 1 , a total flavonoid content (TFC) of 6180.67 ± 94.25 mg CE L - 1 and a DPPH free radical-scavenging capacity of 76.53 ± 3.65 mmol TE L - 1 . Triplicate confirmation experiments validated the model, with an overall prediction accuracy of 97.69%. Ethanol concentration exerted the greatest influence on the grey relational grade (36.28%). Under identical operating conditions, the optimized UAE provided the most balanced extraction performance. It yielded the highest TPC, antioxidant activity, anti-inflammatory activity, and α-amylase inhibition relative to maceration, magnetic stirring, hand-shaking, and reflux, while LC-MS/MS identified quinic and chlorogenic acids as the principal constituents. These results indicate that the UAE optimized through a Taguchi-based CRITIC-weighted GRA is an effective and sustainable strategy for producing bioactive-rich extracts from quince-leaf waste. PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS: This study provides a practical, statistically grounded route for converting quince (Cydonia oblonga Mill.) leaf waste, an abundant agro-industrial by-product, into phenolic-rich extracts using a green, food-grade ultrasound-assisted process. The sequential screening and multi-response optimization framework can be adopted by food, nutraceutical, and functional-ingredient manufacturers to maximize antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and enzyme-inhibitory activities while minimizing solvent and energy use, supporting cost-effective and sustainable valorization of leaf biomass.

title: Bioactive Peptides in Functional Foods: From Production and Validation to Commercialization, Regulatory Hurdles, and Future Prospects.
abstract: Bioactive peptides (BAPs) exhibit a wide range of health-promoting properties, positioning them as key ingredients for the functional food market. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of the BAP landscape, from discovery and production to commercialization and regulation. Conventional and emerging production technologies are critically analyzed, highlighting advancements in enzymatic hydrolysis, microbial fermentation, and physical processing methods like high-pressure and ultrasound-assisted extraction. The multi-tiered validation pipeline, spanning in silico prediction, in vitro screening, and in vivo models, is examined, revealing a significant disconnect between preliminary bioactivity data and demonstrable clinical efficacy, which is a primary cause for regulatory failure. Commercialization is hampered by technical challenges, including poor bioavailability, gastrointestinal instability, and undesirable sensory attributes, which are being addressed by innovative formulation strategies such as nano-encapsulation. A comparative analysis of global regulatory frameworks, particularly the divergent approaches of the US FDA and EU EFSA, underscores the hurdles in substantiating health claims, with a universal demand for rigorous human clinical trials. Finally, the future prospects are explored, identifying critical research gaps and highlighting the transformative potential of AI-driven peptide design and personalized nutrition through nutrigenomics to unlock the full potential of BAPs. The review further links peptide structure to nine major biological activities, critically compares advanced delivery systems and manufacturing scale-up, and extends the regulatory analysis to major Asia-Pacific markets.

title: MR Imaging and Radiomics Features for Predicting Variant Histology of Bladder Cancer: A Single Centre Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: Introduction Compare MRI features of bladder variant histology (VH) and pure urothelial carcinoma (UC) and determine if MRI radiomics features can predict VH. Methods In this retrospective study, cystectomy pathology database search yielded 37 patients with tumours with more than 50% VH and preoperative MRI's. Cystectomy database search yielded 38 consecutive patients with pure UC and preoperative MRI's. Three radiologists characterized MRI T2, diffusion-weighted, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps and postcontrast features of bladder tumours. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using Gwet's agreement and intra-class coefficients. Another radiologist segmented bladder tumours and adjacent perivesical fat on T2-weighted and ADC images using radiomics software. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) was used to determine radiomics features that distinguished VH from UC. Fifty datasets were prepared using multiple imputation approach, and variables were normalized for LASSO variable selection. Results Patients with VH (mean age = 68, 54 (72%) men) included squamous cell (n = 17), sarcomatoid (n = 6), plasmacytoid (n = 6), adenocarcinoma (n = 4) and small cell (n = 4) variants. Inter-reader agreement was similar for VH and UC (p > 0.44). All readers characterized all squamous cell carcinoma as T2 intermediate. For two of three readers, 92%-100% of hypoenhancing tumours were VH at pathology whereas 74%-78% of hyperenhancing masses were UC (p = 0.001). Combination of 11 selected radiomics features had AUC of 0.98 for training and 0.95 for validation data for prediction of VH. Conclusion Squamous cell carcinoma was T2 intermediate, and VH was more likely to hypoenhance compared to UC. Our radiomic model had excellent performance for predicting VH.

title: Impact of Breast Density and Other Factors on Mammography Guided Vacuum Assisted Breast Biopsy Microcalcification Retrieval Rates.
abstract: Introduction Mammography guided vacuum-assisted biopsy (MG-VAB) is the preferred method for histological diagnosis of screening mammography detected microcalcifications, yet the influence of breast density as well as other patient and procedure-specific factors on retrieval remains underexplored. The purpose of this study is to assess the impact of patient and procedure-specific factors on MG-VAB microcalcification retrieval rates. Methods A retrospective cohort study of 803 consecutive MG-VAB procedures for breast calcifications performed between August 2017 and May 2023 in the BreastScreen ACT population was conducted. Patient data collected included age, breast density, compressed breast thickness, lesion quadrant, calcification size, nipple-to-lesion distance, biopsy approach, specimen radiography visibility as well as presence on pathology. Bayesian logistic regression with weakly informative priors was applied to estimate microcalcification retrieval rates (MRR) and 90% credible intervals. Results The overall median MRR was 98.27% (790/803). Retrieval remained high across age groups (96.4%-99.6%), breast density (95.1%-98.7%), lesion quadrants (96.8%-99.1%), biopsy approach (97.9%-98.6%). Continuous factors such as compressed breast thickness, calcification size and nipple-to-lesion distance demonstrated stable retrieval across ranges. Conclusion MG-VAB achieves consistently high microcalcification retrieval rates across a range of patient and procedural factors, including breast density. These findings reinforce its role as the first line diagnostic method for screening detected microcalcifications.

title: From Recall to Reassurance: Common Benign Mimics in Breast Screening Assessment-A Pictorial Review.
abstract: Benign breast lesions, anatomical variants, and imaging artefacts can closely mimic malignancy on screening mammography and are a frequent diagnostic challenge in the assessment setting. This pictorial review showcases a spectrum of benign lesions encountered in a high-volume breast screening assessment setting that initially raised suspicion for malignancy but were subsequently confirmed as benign through a combination of digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT), targeted ultrasound, and clinicopathological correlation. Examples include cutaneous lesions, sebaceous cysts, intramammary lymph nodes, hamartomas, fat necrosis, vascular lesions, simple cysts and summation artefact. Through illustrative cases, we highlight key imaging features that support accurate lesion characterization and demonstrate the complementary roles of mammography, DBT, and ultrasound in distinguishing benign entities from breast cancer. Familiarity with these imaging appearances can improve diagnostic confidence, reduce false-positive recalls, and minimize unnecessary biopsies within breast screening programs.

title: Can Simple MRI Characteristics Predict Molecular Subgroups in Paediatric Medulloblastoma?
abstract: Introduction Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant paediatric central nervous system (CNS) tumour and is classified using molecular subgroups: WNT, SHH and non-WNT/non-SHH. Subgroup identification guides prognosis and treatment, but requires molecular testing, which is not universally available. MRI is routine in assessment of CNS tumours, and the MRI characteristics may serve as surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subgrouping. This study aims to use simple MRI surrogate markers identified by Perreault et al., against local medulloblastoma cases and their final molecular outcome. Method Retrospective cohort study of paediatric medulloblastomas at a single tertiary children's hospital between January 2015 and October 2025. MRI studies were reviewed by a paediatric neuroradiologist and a radiology registrar in consensus. Tumours were classified by location (cerebellar hemisphere, cerebellopontine angle/cerebellar peduncle (CP/CPA), or midline/fourth ventricle) and enhancement pattern (minimal/none = < 10%, heterogeneous = 10%-90%, solid = > 90%). Associations between MRI features and molecular subgroup were assessed. Results Twenty-two cases were analysed: SHH 22.7% (5/22), WNT 13.6% (3/22) and non-WNT/non-SHH 63.7% (14/22). Most tumours were midline (90.9%), with two hemispheric lesions and no CP/CPA. Enhancement patterns were heterogeneous (54.5%), solid (36.4%) and minimal/none (9.1%). Hemispheric location was associated with SHH tumours (p = 0.043), and all WNT tumours demonstrated solid enhancement (p = 0.036). No other statistically significant associations were identified. Conclusion MRI characteristics offer promising surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subtype. The only strong predictor we found corresponding with Perreault et al. is that hemispheric lesions are correlated with SHH-activated medulloblastoma. This supports further investigation of MRI markers as non-invasive and preoperative medulloblastoma subgroup prediction.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Scoring System and Exploratory Multiomics in Ankylosing Spondylitis: Hip Severity and Age-at-Severe-Hip-Involvement Stratification.
abstract: Introduction Accurate diagnosis and assessment of hip involvement are important for the clinical management of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). This study aimed to develop and internally validate an artificial intelligence-based Ensemble Scoring System (ESS) for AS diagnosis and hip-disease severity assessment and to explore its association with heterogeneous immune-cell infiltration and age at first documented severe hip involvement. Methods A total of 5721 patients with pelvic radiographs and linked clinical records were retrospectively included. Participants were divided into training and held-out validation cohorts at a 7:3 ratio strictly at the patient level, with no patient or image overlap. Deep-learning features extracted by a convolutional neural network were integrated with clinical variables using XGBoost to construct task-specific ensemble deep-learning (EDL) models. Exploratory proteomic, transcriptomic, single-cell RNA-sequencing, immunohistochemical, and peripheral-blood analyses were performed to investigate AS-related immune infiltration. An exploratory immune ensemble (IE) score was constructed using the monocyte proportion and EDL score. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to examine the association between the IE score and age at severe hip involvement. Results The EDL model achieved AUCs of 0.978 for distinguishing AS from non-AS, 0.990 for identifying hip arthropathy among patients with AS, and 0.996 for identifying BASRI-Hip grade ≥ 3 among patients with hip arthropathy. Monocyte percentage was an influential feature across the three EDL classification tasks. Exploratory multiomics and immunohistochemical analyses showed higher LYN expression in AS than in the corresponding non-AS fracture-control groups and suggested that LYN expression was concentrated predominantly in monocytes. A high IE score was associated with earlier severe hip involvement, with estimated median ages at first documented severe hip involvement of 36 and 50 years in the high- and low-IE-score groups, respectively. This finding represents exploratory risk stratification and does not establish independent prediction of biological disease progression. Conclusions The ESS showed strong internal validation performance for AS diagnosis and hip-disease severity classification. Exploratory analyses linked LYN dysregulation in monocytes with heterogeneous immune infiltration, while the IE score was associated with earlier severe hip involvement. Prospective multicenter external validation is required before clinical application.

title: Nodule Dye-Localization Using Interventional Fluoroscopy for Image-Guided Sublobar Lung Resection.
abstract: Background Precise localization is critical for sublobar resection of small pulmonary nodules. We evaluated the safety, technical efficiency, and clinical outcomes of preoperative percutaneous dye-localization using a cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-enabled flat-panel detector interventional fluoroscopy system in a hybrid operating room (HOR). Methods We retrospectively reviewed 74 consecutive patients (137 lesions) who underwent image-guided localization followed by video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) sublobar resection (wedge resection or segmentectomy) between 2022 and 2023 at Chia-Yi Christian Hospital. Procedural workflow, localization success, surgical margins, and perioperative outcomes were systematically analyzed. Results Technical localization success was achieved in 100% of lesions (mean nodule diameter: 8.59 ± 4.85 mm). The procedure required a mean of 1.31 ± 0.67 puncture attempts per lesion at a mean depth of 5.22 ± 1.86 cm. Procedure-related pneumothorax occurred in 29.7% (22/74) of patients, with 14.9% (11/74) requiring pigtail catheter drainage; pneumothorax occurrence was significantly associated with multiple puncture attempts (p < 0.001) and lower-lobe lesions (p = 0.001). Lower-lobe location was significantly associated with requiring more puncture attempts (p = 0.028). For malignant lesions, the mean pathological resection margin was 17.16 ± 8.73 mm, with 92.31% achieving a margin-to-tumor ratio (MTR) ≥ 1. The mean postoperative hospital stay was 3.04 ± 1.16 days. Conclusions Single-stage image-guided dye-localization and VATS sublobar lung resection in an HOR using a biplane CBCT-enabled platform is safe, feasible, and effective. This streamlined workflow ensures high technical success and adequate surgical margins with manageable complications. Further studies are warranted to evaluate long-term oncological outcomes.

title: Machine Learning-Based Screening for Osteonecrosis of the Jaw in Panoramic Radiographs.
abstract: Background Osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ) is a serious condition associated mainly with antiresorptive therapy and maxillofacial radiotherapy. As detection of its radiographic findings may facilitate patient referral, this study aimed to develop convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for ONJ screening in panoramic radiographs (OPGs). Methods A dataset of 888 ONJ-positive OPGs and 888 ONJ-negative controls was assembled and annotated using bounding boxes. The dataset was split at patient level 70-10-20 for training, validation, and testing. Multiple CNNs (ResNet18, ResNet34, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0) were trained on cropped image regions and evaluated using standard performance metrics. Performance on full OPGs (without cropping) was tested, and subgroup analysis was performed. Regions contributing to model predictions were visualised using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). Results EfficientNet-B0 performed best, with per-crop accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score of 92.24%, 89.80%, 94.69%, 94.42% and 82.05%, respectively. At 0.9 probability threshold, per-image accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score equalled 76.65%. Grad-CAM highlighted clinically relevant regions; however, differentiation from other changes in bone density was suboptimal. Conclusions Despite promising results at crop level, model performance in full OPG analysis is currently insufficient for clinical application. Further optimisation of localisation strategies and external validation are needed for reliable clinical application.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Dentistry: A Scoping Review.
abstract: This review scoped artificial intelligence (AI) in paediatric dentistry to summarize current applications and limitations. A comprehensive literature search was completed across PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, Embase, IEEE Xplore, and medRxiv/aArXiv. The preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) checklist was used for reporting the present study. Studies concerning paediatric dentistry and utilizing AI, machine learning (ML) or large language models (LLMs) were included. Two independent reviewers screened and three extracted data on AI methodologies, performance metrics, and clinical applications. Fifty-nine studies were included. Computer vision studies (n = 32) most often used panoramic radiographs (n = 14), mainly for tooth detection, numbering and segmentation (n = 10) and caries detection (n = 9). Non-imaging ML studies (n = 18) primarily used clinical variables and questionnaire data (n = 8) or salivary/biological samples (n = 10). Accuracy ranged from 50% to 100%, with sensitivity reaching 100% in biomarker-based studies. LLM accuracy varied widely (33%-96%). Computer vision and non-imaging ML show promise for paediatric dentistry, particularly in the detection of dental structures and diseases, as well as risk stratification. Variable LLM performance underscores the need for standardized evaluation before clinical integration. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: AI-based tools may support paediatric dentists by improving tooth detection, dental structure assessment, caries detection, disease prediction and risk stratification. Computer vision and non-imaging machine learning approaches appear to have potential, but their clinical value depends on robust external validation, transparent reporting and integration into paediatric dental workflows. Given their variable performance, AI tools should be used only as adjunctive tools or a second reviewer.

title: Morphological, Radiographic and Three-Dimensional Scanning Characterization of the Skull and Mandible of the American Crocodile (Crocodylus acutus).
abstract: The American crocodile (Crocodylus acutus) is a widely distributed Neotropical species for which detailed osteological descriptions of the skull and mandible remain scarce. This study provides an integrative characterization of the cranial and mandibular complex using gross anatomy, descriptive cranial morphometry, radiography, and three-dimensional (3D) scanning. Four skulls and mandibles from post mortem specimens were prepared following standard osteological procedures, and descriptive cranial measurements were recorded. Radiographic projection allowed visualization of bone margins, cranial sutures, dental alveoli, fenestrae, and articular regions. Three-dimensional models generated through a structured-light 3D scanning workflow documented external contours, choanal margins, temporal and mandibular fenestrae, alveolar borders, and sutural patterns. In dorsal, ventral, lateral, and caudal views, the examined skulls displayed an elongated rostrum, dorsally positioned orbits and external nares, paired supratemporal and lateral temporal fenestrae, and a single occipital condyle. The mandibles exhibited elongated and firmly fused symphyses, pronounced retroarticular processes, and well-defined internal and external mandibular fenestrae. Dental preservation varied among specimens, but tooth spacing, conical morphology, and rostrocaudal size variation could be documented in the preserved series. These findings provide a specimen-based reference for the cranial and mandibular complex of C. acutus by integrating morphological, morphometric, radiographic, and three-dimensional (3D) scanning evidence. The digital models constitute an additional resource for anatomical teaching, comparative studies, and long-term digital documentation of osteological morphology.

title: Investigating Artificial Intelligence Performance on Mammographic Cases in High- and Low-Resourced Countries.
abstract: Population-based screening in Australia for breast cancer using mammography has delivered key outcomes in reducing deaths, but such programs are usually not present in Vietnam. Breast cancer is common in both countries, with Vietnamese women having high breast density and Vietnam having low radiology expertise. This paper investigated the performance of two state-of-the-art Artificial Intelligence (AI) models for cancer detection on Datasets 1 and 2 (Vietnam and Australian mammographic cases) and determined whether the breast density in the two datasets with different vendors affected the AI performance. Both datasets consisted of the same number of mammographic cases (865 malignant; 865 normal). Mammographic images were enhanced using the contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization algorithm. Transfer learning of the Globally-aware Multiple Instance Classifier (GMIC) and Global-Local Activation Maps (GLAM) AI models was conducted on enhanced images in the two national datasets. The breast density was classified as four levels (A, B, C, and D) by three radiologists. We combined Levels A and B into 0%-50%, and Levels C and D into 50%-100% breast density. The performance of these two AI models, both with and without transfer learning, was evaluated on the two datasets using McNemar's test. The GMIC in the pre-trained and transfer learning modes outperformed the GLAM in terms of specificity and sensitivity in the two datasets. The performance of the GMIC and GLAM with transfer learning in Dataset 2 was better, with 86.7% specificity and 88.2% sensitivity, outperforming their transfer learning model with 80.4% specificity and 81.2% sensitivity in Dataset 1. The specificity and sensitivity of the two AI models (p-values <0.05) were significantly improved using transfer learning in the two datasets. The specificity and sensitivity of GMIC with transfer learning (p-values <0.05) on the 0%-50% and 50%-100% breast density in Dataset 2 were significantly higher than those in Dataset 1, respectively.

title: Emerging Roles of Gold Nanoparticles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis and Imaging: A Promising yet Underexplored Frontier.
abstract: Cancer is known to be a major cause of death worldwide, with lung cancer responsible for the maximum number of deaths. There is an urgent need for early and effective diagnosis of lung cancer to improve the overall survival rate, which is extremely low to date. Studies have shown that 57% of lung cancers are detected only after metastasis of the tumor. Economic restraints in hospitals are resulting in decreased early diagnosis of lung cancer and an increase in aggressive, incurable grades. Traditional imaging modalities like ultrasound, x-ray, CT, and MRI scans are often unable to precisely locate the extent of metastasis of lung cancer, paving the way for better, more sophisticated diagnostic tools. Nuclear medicine techniques help in better understanding of the metabolic extent of cancer cells using radioactive isotopes. PET/SPECT scans help provide more precise grading and better understanding of tumor morphology. However, the lack of distinction between inflammatory and malignant lesions remains a diagnostic challenge. Gold nanoparticles (GNPs) have been studied as effective contrast agents, enhancing the diagnostic efficiency of lung cancer. Formulation and tagging of GNPs have improved efficacy and biodistribution of cancer drugs; however, no such gold nanoformulation is available for diagnosis to date. The use of different shapes of GNPs functionalized with specific lung cancer biomarkers can potentially increase the specificity of lung tumor diagnosis. In this review, we address the lacunae and provide a strategic roadmap for the effective development of GNP-based diagnostics, from benchtop to high-fidelity biomaterials with clinical applications for efficient lung cancer management.

title: Transvaginal Ultrasound for Endometriosis: Learning From a Decade of Diagnostic Challenges Through a Retrospective Observational Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Endometriosis is a chronic, inflammatory condition associated with pelvic pain, subfertility, and reduced quality of life. Advances in enhanced transvaginal ultrasound (eTVUS), including systematic compartment-based scanning protocols and improved operator training, have increased diagnostic accuracy, particularly for deep endometriosis. Aims To evaluate and critically reflect on the diagnostic performance of eTVUS during its implementation prior to the adoption of standardised scanning protocols. Using the #ENZIAN classification system, the diagnostic performance of eTVUS was assessed by comparing ultrasound findings with laparoscopic visualisation as the reference standard. Methods A retrospective observational study of patients with suspected endometriosis who underwent preoperative eTVUS and subsequent laparoscopy between January 2015 and January 2024 at a single tertiary hospital. Ultrasound and surgical findings were mapped to #ENZIAN compartments and grades. Agreement and diagnostic metrics were calculated using laparoscopy as the reference standard. Results Among 221 patients with paired ultrasound and laparoscopy, adnexal endometriomas were detected with a sensitivity of 81.4% and specificity of 84.1%. Tubo-ovarian complex disease demonstrated a sensitivity of 72.9% and specificity of 68.8%. Sensitivity for deep endometriosis was lower, with specificity for detection depending on anatomical location varying from 83%-95%. Bladder involvement had a PPV of 83.3% and NPV of 94.8%; ureteric disease had a PPV of 0% and NPV of ~100%. Peritoneal disease was rarely identified. Conclusion eTVUS demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for ovarian endometriomas, moderate performance for bowel involvement, and low sensitivity for peritoneal disease.
